# Test: hasPeerOffer liveness-aware staleness

Test-first spec for parent AC7: entries older than `DEFAULT_DOWNTIME_MARKER_STALE_WINDOW_MS` must count as absent peers at both orchestrator call sites, while fresh entries keep cancelling the no-candidate cooldown; `pruneStaleEntries` stays a deliberate no-op.

## Impact

Users with idle downtime leaders can now reliably discover and dispatch work from roots where other herdr instances may have crashed or gone offline, because stale coordination entries no longer masquerade as live peers.

## Acceptance Criteria

- \`hasPeerOffer\` is made liveness-aware (rejects entries older than \`DEFAULT_DOWNTIME_MARKER_STALE_WINDOW_MS\`), and the decision is recorded in code comments and docs; entry expiry remains a no-op (parent AC7).
- An entry whose \`lastUpdated\` is older than \`DEFAULT_DOWNTIME_MARKER_STALE_WINDOW_MS\` is treated as no peer at both orchestrator call sites (orchestrator-tick and orchestrator-dispatch) (AC7).
- A fresh peer entry still satisfies \`hasPeerOffer\`, so peer-offer cooldown cancellation is unchanged for live instances.
- The instance's own entry and the leader block never count as a peer; \`pruneStaleEntries\` returns 0 and never mutates the coordination file (no-op contract).
- Callers without explicit staleness arguments keep the default window — the signature change is additive.
- The conservative rationale (stale = absent peer makes the leader more willing to sweep, never less) is asserted in code comments and the dispatcher doc (AC7 last clause).

## Key Files

# Generalise the host dispatch budget to any work item type

## Problem Statement

The host-wide dispatch budget (`packages/herdr/src/host-dispatch-budget.ts`,
parent WL-0MVXWQFGV000D2AB) only covers two kinds: `implement` and `audit`.
`budget.json` is a fixed two-field shape (`{ "maxImplement": 2, "maxAudit": 1 }`),
the `HostBudgetKind` type is `'implement' | 'audit'`, and the interactive
over-quota dialog (`budgetKindForAgentCommand`) recognises only those two.
Capping `plan`, `intake` or `risk-effort` dispatches is currently impossible —
it was explicitly recorded as out of scope in the v1 contract (F6,
WL-0MVXY10QH0020V7S: "Capping the `plan` / `intake` / `risk-effort` tiers is
likewise out of scope").

Operators want one machine-scoped concurrency governor that can cap any kind
of dispatched work, with the same semantics the implement/audit tiers already
have — and they want it to be a general mechanism, not N special cases.

## Users

- **Operators.** As a herdr operator, I want to set a host-wide concurrency
  cap for any dispatch kind (`implement`, `audit`, `plan`, `intake`,
  `risk-effort`), so that I can bound the machine's agent work-in-flight per
  kind — and leave any kind unlimited by simply not configuring it.
- **Downtime dispatcher.** As the dispatch admission path, I want one generic
  budget check for every kind, so plan/intake/risk-effort dispatches are
  subject to the same host-wide constraints (and the same observability) as
  implement/audit.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Any kind configurable.** `budget.json` accepts a cap for every dispatch
   kind (`implement`, `audit`, `plan`, `intake`, `risk-effort`). A cap set
   for any kind is enforced at admission (refuse when live >= cap) on both
   dispatcher paths (direct and coordination leader), with `0` remaining the
   per-kind kill switch.
2. **Absent = unlimited.** A kind not explicitly present in the budget config
   is **unlimited**: admission never refuses it on budget grounds, it is never
   counted against any cap, and its dispatches are not recorded in the ledger
   (no reserve/release bookkeeping for uncapped kinds). No default cap is
   invented for unconfigured kinds.
3. **Existing budgets preserved.** The default stays `implement: 2`,
   `audit: 1`, and an operator's existing `budget.json` values keep their
   meaning and enforcement (same refusal behaviour, same kill switch) — the
   generalisation must not change or silently drop configured caps.
4. **Counting asymmetry preserved, audit-only.** Only `audit` keeps the
   over-hold semantics: it counts fresh ledger entries with **no** live-pane
   requirement (`freshCount` — slot held from reservation until a release
   point fires or the 2 h stale window). Every **other** kind counts only
   fresh entries whose pane is in the machine-wide live pane list
   (`liveCount`), so its slot frees when the pane leaves the live list.
5. **Legacy code removed (no backward compatibility).** The following are
   deleted, not kept behind compat shims:
   - the retired `active-audit` marker readers (`readActiveAuditMarker`,
     `isHostAuditActive` in `machine-coordination.ts`) and the synthetic
     legacy-marker entry count (`legacyActiveAuditCount` / `reduceMarkerCounts`);
   - the `audit-host-saturated` token special-case at `maxAudit: 1`
     (unified to the single `host-budget-audit` refusal token);
   - the fixed two-kind `HostBudgetKind` type and `DEFAULT_HOST_BUDGET_CONFIG`
     shape; the fixed two-key env overrides (`HERDR_HOST_MAX_IMPLEMENT` /
     `HERDR_HOST_MAX_AUDIT`) are generalised or removed;
   - any F6 doc carve-out text describing plan/intake/risk-effort as out of
     scope.
   A repo-wide scan confirms no references to the removed symbols remain
   (module headers, doc comments and the `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`
   contract of record updated to match).
6. **Interactive over-quota gate generalised.** A hand-fired
   `/skill:<kind>` dispatch for any capped kind consults the same ledger/cap
   and prompts on over-quota, exactly as implement/audit do today
   (`budgetKindForAgentCommand` generalised to all kinds).
7. **Observability generalised.** The worklist header counter, stderr skip
   line and decision-log tokens report live/max **per configured kind**
   (any capped kind), never for uncapped kinds; an uncapped kind can never
   produce a budget refusal token.
8. **Tests.** Unit + integration tests cover: capped plan/intake/risk-effort
   admit and refuse at their caps; an uncapped kind always admits and records
   nothing; per-kind kill switch `0`; audit over-hold vs live-pane release
   for all other kinds; refusal tokens unified (no `audit-host-saturated`
   anywhere); legacy-marker references gone; existing implement/audit
   behaviour with the default config unchanged. Full project suite passes.

## Constraints

- Scope: `packages/herdr` only (ledger, admission, interactive gate,
  observability, machine-coordination). No worklog (`wl`) / database scoring
  changes; the dispatcher head remains the sole ranking path.
- `scheduled` prompts are **not** a work-item kind and stay outside the
  budget; the budget covers `DowntimeSkillKind` only.
- The budget remains the **outer** concurrency governor: the inner capacity
  gates (free-slot minimums, local reservation/prefill pacing, contention,
  host-CPU gate) keep their existing order and meaning.
- No `window`/rate-limit field (explicitly still out of scope in v1).

## Existing State

- `HostBudgetKind = 'implement' | 'audit'` (`host-dispatch-budget.ts`),
  `DEFAULT_HOST_BUDGET_CONFIG = { maxImplement: 2, maxAudit: 1 }`, clamps
  `0..HOST_BUDGET_MAX (32)`, env overrides `HERDR_HOST_MAX_IMPLEMENT` /
  `HERDR_HOST_MAX_AUDIT`.
- Counting: implement uses `liveCount` (live-pane), audit uses `freshCount`
  (marker semantics, incl. the synthetic legacy-marker entry).
- Admission in `host-dispatch-budget.admission.ts`
  (`admitHostDispatch` / `readAuditBudgetState` / `confirmHostDispatch` /
  `releaseHostDispatch`); interactive gate in
  `host-dispatch-budget.interactive.ts`; refuse tokens
  `host-budget-implement` / `host-budget-audit` / `host-budget-unknown` plus
  the `audit-host-saturated` compat token.
- The removal of the legacy `active-audit` readers was already scheduled for
  "the release after the host-wide budget generalisation ships"
  (`docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`, F6 removal schedule) — this item is
  that release.
- `DowntimeSkillKind = 'plan' | 'intake' | 'audit' | 'implement' |
  'risk-effort'`; dispatch-classified kinds today are `audit`, `implement`,
  `plan`, `intake` (intake → plan → implement chain) and `risk-effort`
  (effort/risk evaluation for plan_complete items).

## Desired Change

1. Generalise `HostBudgetKind` to all `DowntimeSkillKind` members; the config
   becomes a map over kinds (absent kind ⇒ uncapped). Keep `implement: 2`,
   `audit: 1` as the defaults for those kinds.
2. Admission becomes one generic path: look up the kind's cap; absent ⇒ admit
   without reservation; present ⇒ the existing live-count admission with the
   audit over-hold exception (`freshCount` for `audit` only).
3. Delete the legacy-marker surface and unify the refusal tokens on
   `host-budget-*`.
4. Extend `budgetKindForAgentCommand` and the over-quota dialog to all kinds.
5. Generalise the observability surfaces (counter, skip line, decision tokens)
   to list every configured kind; uncapped kinds never appear.
6. Update `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` (module tables, gate table,
   removal schedule, out-of-scope wording) and all affected module doc
   comments.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/host-dispatch-budget.ts` — kind type, config schema,
  live/fresh counting, reap, kill switch
- `packages/herdr/src/host-dispatch-budget.admission.ts` — generic admission,
  refusal tokens, audit over-hold
- `packages/herdr/src/host-dispatch-budget.interactive.ts` /
  `host-budget-dialog.ts` — over-quota gate + dialog for all kinds
- `packages/herdr/src/machine-coordination.ts` — remove legacy marker readers
- `packages/herdr/src/host-budget-status.ts` — generalised counter/skip line
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.constants.ts` — refusal-token mapping
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — contract of record update
- Tests: `host-dispatch-budget*.test.ts`, `host-budget-dialog*.test.ts`,
  `downtime-worker.dispatch.test.ts`, `index.test.ts`, machine tests

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Assumption (recorded):** "Keep the configured budget for any existing
  items in place" means the default caps (`implement: 2`, `audit: 1`) and any
  operator-written `budget.json` values remain honoured exactly; the
  generalisation may change the on-disk schema but must preserve the effective
  caps and enforcement for `implement` and `audit`.
- **Assumption (recorded):** uncapped kinds bypass the ledger entirely (no
  reserve/release entries) — simplest semantics for "not limited"; the
  pane-close release is idempotent by item id and unaffected for capped kinds.
- Risk: generalising the admission seam touches the dispatch choke point;
  mitigated by keeping the counting asymmetry behaviour-preserving for
  implement/audit and by the test matrix (AC8).
- Risk: observability surfaces must not regress for existing kinds — the
  unified `host-budget-audit` token replaces `audit-host-saturated`, so any
  operator tooling keyed on the old token must be updated in the same change.

## Related Work

- WL-0MVXWQFGV000D2AB (completed) — parent: host-wide concurrency budget for
  implement and audit dispatches (this item extends it)
- WL-0MVXY0XPF006YUHA (completed) — F2 audit 1→N generalisation + active-audit
  unification, which scheduled the legacy-marker removal this item performs
- WL-0MVXY0WQF0069YDJ / WL-0MVXY0YG7009JMHI / WL-0MVXY0Z93002HKCZ /
  WL-0MVXY0ZYW009NEJD / WL-0MVXY10QH0020V7S / WL-0MVXY11IL0032S07
  (completed) — F1–F7 slices of the original budget work

---
*Created from a user request to extend the budget workflow to any work item
type, with unlimited default for unconfigured kinds, no backward-compatibility
requirement (dead code removal permitted), existing budgets preserved, and the
over-hold approach retained for audit only.*

## Plan

Decomposition into 7 test-first vertical slices (parent ACs folded into each child as traceability ACs; deps wired T1→F1→F2→F3 and F1→F4, F2/F4→F5, F3/F5→F6):

| ID | Title | Slice | Depends on |
|----|-------|-------|-----------|
| WL-0MWF33QKQ002H17E (T1) | Generalised-budget test matrix (tests-first) | Tests pinning the target behaviour (red first) | — |
| WL-0MWF33ZB0000RC88 (F1) | Kind-generalised config & ledger | `HostBudgetKind`→all kinds; kind-named `budget.json` + legacy `max*` read-compat; defaults preserved; `HERDR_HOST_MAX_<KIND>` | T1 |
| WL-0MWF34932000SNTX (F2) | Generic admission + audit-only over-hold | One admission path on both dispatcher paths; audit `freshCount` over-hold only; unified `host-budget-<kind>` tokens | F1 |
| WL-0MWF34IEP00221NU (F3) | Legacy marker & token removal | Delete `active-audit` readers/synthetic count + `audit-host-saturated`; repo-wide scan | F2 |
| WL-0MWF34P5G006QOOX (F4) | Interactive gate for all kinds | `budgetKindForAgentCommand` → all kinds; over-quota dialog for capped kinds | F1 |
| WL-0MWF351XL002WVL2 (F5) | Observability per configured kind | Header/skip-line/tokens report live/max per configured kind; uncapped invisible | F2, F4 |
| WL-0MWF359A8005ZRF4 (F6) | Docs & contract of record | `downtime-dispatcher.md`, README, headers; F6 carve-out removed | F3, F5 |

Sizing: each slice is a minimal end-to-end increment (code + tests + doc comments). T1 is the tests-first slice per the plan skill; F6 is the deliberate final docs-only contract-of-record slice.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Q1 — budget.json schema: how do per-kind caps appear on disk? (A) kind-named keys with legacy max* read-compat; (B) extend max* camelCase convention." Answer (operator): "1. A" — kind-named keys (`{ "implement": 2, ... }`) with legacy `maxImplement`/`maxAudit` read-compat so existing files keep meaning; `DEFAULT_HOST_BUDGET_CONFIG` becomes `{ implement: 2, audit: 1 }`. Final: A. Recorded 2026-11-13.
- Q: "Q2 — env overrides: generalise or remove? (A) generalise to HERDR_HOST_MAX_<KIND> keeping the two existing names; (B) remove entirely." Answer (operator): "2. A" — generalise to `HERDR_HOST_MAX_<KIND>` for all five kinds; the existing two keys stay valid. Final: A. Recorded 2026-11-13.
- OPEN QUESTION: none.

## Impact

An operator can now cap any kind of host dispatch — plan, intake and risk-effort as well as implement and audit — from one `budget.json`, leave any kind unlimited simply by not configuring it, and see every capped kind's live/max in the worklist header and the over-quota dialog.

# Dispatcher claims work items as 'dispatcher' instead of producer sentinel 'Map'

## Problem statement

The herdr downtime dispatcher claims every work item it auto-dispatches with the
producer sentinel `Map`, so an auto-dispatched claim is indistinguishable from a
deliberate producer hold. Agent sessions preserve it at exit, the TTL reaper never
reaps it, and the item is stranded as a scheduling hold with no agent working.

Observed on WL-0MVR8GDJ3008WY3Y: the herdr worker claimed it with `Map` at intake
dispatch (02:06 UTC) and again at plan dispatch (~13:03 UTC). The plan session
completed (stage `plan_complete`, status `open`) but deliberately restored `Map`
believing it was a producer hold. The item has stayed invisible to dispatch ever
since (`wl next` skips held items; the all-held dispatch window is only surfaced
read-only, WL-0MVR8FN1D002SCIR).

## Users

- **Producer / operator** — needs auto-dispatched work to keep flowing after a
  session ends; a stranded `Map` claim silently stalls the queue.
- **Herdr downtime dispatcher** — claims items before spawning agent panes; needs
  an identity that means "an agent is on it", not "the producer parked it".
- **Agent sessions (intake/plan/implement/audit/risk-effort)** — release their own
  claims at session end; must release a dispatcher claim exactly like an agent
  claim, while never touching a genuine producer hold.
- **Auditor / reviewer** — relies on `needsProducerReview` and the `Map` hold as
  the only two legitimate reasons an item is intentionally held.

Example user stories:

- As the producer, when the dispatcher claims an item and the session ends without
  completing it, the item becomes dispatchable again instead of vanishing.
- As an agent session, I preserve a `Map` producer hold at exit but clear a
  `dispatcher` claim, so I never strand auto-dispatched work.
- As the downtime worker, I can distinguish "held by the producer on purpose" from
  "claimed by me moments ago" without reading the source.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1**: `packages/herdr/src/index.claim.ts` claims auto-dispatched items with `dispatcher` (replacing `AGENT_ASSIGNEE = 'Map'`), for every dispatch tier (audit, implement, plan, intake, risk-effort) and every dispatch path that uses `claimWorkItem` / `claimItem`.
- **AC2**: An assignee of `dispatcher` is not a scheduling hold: `wl next` / dispatch gates / the herdr assignee-hold filter (`downtime-worker.offer-attribution.ts` / `downtime-worker.selection.ts` `isAssigneeHeld`) never skip an item merely because its assignee is `dispatcher`.
- **AC3**: Agent sessions release the `dispatcher` claim on every terminal outcome — the shared `should_release_assignee` predicate and `release_session_claim` / `reap_stale_claims` backstops treat `dispatcher` as releasable (it is not a protected producer hold).
- **AC4**: A genuine producer hold (`Map` / `WORKLOG_PRODUCER_ASSIGNEE`) remains sacrosanct: never released, never reaped, still a scheduling hold. Existing behaviour for `Map` is unchanged.
- **AC5**: The producer-assignee sentinel and the dispatcher claim identity are defined once each in code (configurable or a shared constant) so the two concepts cannot drift again; the collision is documented in code comments at both call sites.
- **AC6**: Tests cover: dispatcher claims record `dispatcher`; a `dispatcher`-held item is still dispatchable / not held; a `dispatcher` claim is released by `should_release_assignee` and by the session backstop; a `Map` producer hold is still preserved; the all-held-window attribution no longer counts `dispatcher` as a hold.
- **AC7**: All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, `AGENTS.md` / the global agent instructions, and `docs/dev/assignee-release.md` / `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`.
- **AC8**: Full project test suite must pass with the new changes; no regression in the herdr dispatch/offer suites.

## Constraints

- **Cross-repo scope.** The herdr claim identity lives in this repository (ContextHub, `packages/herdr`). The shared Python release predicate (`skill/shared/claim_release.py` — `PRODUCER_ASSIGNEE_DEFAULT`, `is_producer_assignee`, `should_release_assignee`, `release_session_claim`, `reap_stale_claims`) is agent infrastructure that in this checkout resolves through `skill/shared -> ~/.pi/agent/skills/shared`, i.e. the **SorraAgents** repository. `docs/dev/assignee-release.md` and `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` also live in SorraAgents. The fix therefore spans two repositories, and the ContextHub item may need a posed, blocking SorraAgents companion item for the Python-side predicate, docs and release invariant wording.
- Do not weaken any safety gate: `dispatcher` is only ever the claim identity, never a bypass. `needsProducerReview` and producer-hold semantics stay exactly as-is.
- The agent-side release logic (skill/shared) is shared infrastructure — prefer a single predicate that knows both identities (`dispatcher` releasable, `Map` protected), rather than a second ad-hoc check.
- Keep existing `Map` producer-hold behaviour byte-for-byte; treat any change to `Map` semantics as a regression.
- Do not edit agent infrastructure under `.pi/` or the symlinked `skill/shared` unless the cross-repo work is explicitly authorised in the SorraAgents checkout.

## Existing state

- `packages/herdr/src/index.claim.ts` — `const AGENT_ASSIGNEE = 'Map'`; used by `claimItemForAgentCommand` (`claimWorkItem(itemId, AGENT_ASSIGNEE)`) and re-exported.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts:1589` — `createDowntimeDeps(SEND_TO_PI_SCRIPT, AGENT_ASSIGNEE)` feeds the same constant into the downtime claim path (`deps.claimItem`), so the dispatcher and interactive claims currently share the `Map` identity.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.dispatch-claims.ts` — the claim → marker → spawn pipeline; `claimItem` CAS semantics; no assignee policy of its own.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.selection.ts` — `isAssigneeHeld` treats **any** non-empty assignee as a hold (`.filter((c) => !isAssigneeHeld(c))` in every dispatch candidate path).
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.offer-attribution.ts` — classifies every all-held window solely on a non-empty assignee, with `heldAssignees` (e.g. `['Map']`).
- `skill/shared/claim_release.py` (SorraAgents) — `PRODUCER_ASSIGNEE_DEFAULT = "Map"`, `is_producer_assignee`, `should_release_assignee`; `release_session_claim` and `reap_stale_claims` never touch a producer hold.
- Tests currently hard-code `'Map'` in many dispatch/offer suites (`claim.test.ts`, `coordination-dispatch.test.ts`, `dispatch-window-hold.test.ts`, `worklist-icon-truncation.test.ts`, `index.test.ts`) — these encode the current, incorrect assumption and will need review.

## Desired change

Introduce a distinct `dispatcher` claim identity. The dispatcher claims with
`dispatcher`; an assignee of `dispatcher` is released on every terminal outcome
and is **not** a scheduling hold, so the dispatch gates/offer attribution must
not treat it as held. Keep `Map` (and `WORKLOG_PRODUCER_ASSIGNEE`) as the only
protected producer hold. Define both identities once so they cannot drift, and
document the collision at both call sites and in the release-invariant docs.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk — regression in dispatch gating.** Relaxing `isAssigneeHeld` for `dispatcher` touches the hot path of every candidate filter; mitigate by keeping the predicate single-sourced and adding a test per dispatch path. Residual risk: a `dispatcher` string typo could still be read as a hold, so define the identity as one exported constant.
- **Risk — cross-repo drift.** The Python predicate (SorraAgents) and the TypeScript constant (ContextHub) could disagree about which identities are releasable; mitigate by keeping the sentinel/identity definitions and the collision comment in both places, and by linking the companion SorraAgents item as a blocker.
- **Risk — masked stale claims.** If the dispatcher is killed before a session starts, a `dispatcher` claim could be reaped by the TTL sweep mid-dispatch; the reaper's non-terminal/TTL guard is assumed sufficient (same behaviour as any agent claim).
- **Assumption:** `dispatcher` does not collide with a real agent or producer identity, and is not a value `WORKLOG_PRODUCER_ASSIGNEE` is expected to take.
- **Assumption:** existing `Map` producer-hold behaviour must be preserved exactly; any behavioural change to `Map` is out of scope and a regression.
- **Scope-creep risk:** a wider producer-hold retirement or a general hold-bucket taxonomy is *not* part of this item. Record such opportunities as linked work items rather than expanding scope.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/index.claim.ts` — replace `AGENT_ASSIGNEE = 'Map'` with the dispatcher identity; use a shared constant
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — `createDowntimeDeps(...)` wiring; update comments
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.dispatch-claims.ts` — dispatch claim identity if it is threaded separately
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.selection.ts` — `isAssigneeHeld` must not treat `dispatcher` as a hold
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.offer-attribution.ts` — all-held-window attribution must not count `dispatcher`
- `packages/herdr/src/*.test.ts` — claim/selection/offer-attribution regression tests
- SorraAgents: `skill/shared/claim_release.py` — `should_release_assignee` / `is_producer_assignee` knows `dispatcher` is releasable
- SorraAgents: `docs/dev/assignee-release.md`, `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md`, and this repo's `AGENTS.md` — release-invariant wording gains the `dispatcher` identity
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — dispatcher claim identity documentation

## Related work

- **WL-0MVR8GDJ3008WY3Y** — Downtime leader cannot see a worklog root with no running herdr instance (stranded at `plan_complete` with a lingering `Map` dispatcher claim). This item is `discovered-from` that one.
- **WL-0MVR8FN1D002SCIR** — All-held dispatch window surfaced read-only (the symptom this collision feeds into).
- **WL-0MW51P7FO003AC74** — herdr extension key chords to set the assignee (the manual producer/agent/dispatcher-hold workflow that makes the three identities explicit).
- **WL-0MV85WDOM007BKF8** — Assignee-hold scheduling convention and producer sentinel (established `Map` as the producer sentinel; this item fixes its misuse by the dispatcher). Completed.
- **WL-0MV85WESL002SD0F** — Ship release gate re-homed onto the assignee hold. Completed.
- **WL-0MVAPF19Q0096EP0** — Theme/interview/shortcuts restore + producer-hold retirement. Completed.
- Potentially related docs: `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`, `packages/herdr/README.md`, `CLI.md`, and SorraAgents' `docs/dev/assignee-release.md`.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Duplicate-work check** — Searched `wl search "dispatcher claim assignee Map"`. Closest completed items (WL-0MV85WDOM007BKF8, WL-0MV85WESL002SD0F, WL-0MVAPF19Q0096EP0) define the producer-hold convention and release gate, but none fixes the dispatcher's use of `Map` as its claim identity. No full duplicate; this item addresses the distinct gap. *(Evidence: repo + worklog search, this session.)*
- **Q: Is the shared `should_release_assignee` predicate in this repo?** — Answer (agent, repo inspection): No. In this checkout `skill/shared` is a symlink to `~/.pi/agent/skills/shared`, i.e. the **SorraAgents** repository; `claim_release.py`, `status_lifecycle.py`, `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` and `docs/dev/assignee-release.md` all live there. Only `packages/herdr` is in ContextHub. *(Evidence: `ls -la skill`, `find` for `claim_release*`, `git remote -v`.)* This is recorded as a constraint and may require a blocking SorraAgents companion item.
- **Q: Which tiers dispatch through `AGENT_ASSIGNEE`?** — Answer (agent, code inspection): `claimItemForAgentCommand` (interactive agent commands) and the downtime dispatcher via `createDowntimeDeps(SEND_TO_PI_SCRIPT, AGENT_ASSIGNEE)` at `index.ts:1589`, which reaches `deps.claimItem` in `downtime-worker.dispatch-claims.ts`. A single constant change covers both, but tests that hard-code `'Map'` must be reviewed. *(Evidence: `grep -rn AGENT_ASSIGNEE`, `createDowntimeDeps`.)*

# herdr extension key chords to set a work item's assignee

Add herdr worklist key chords (same mechanism as the existing `c q` quick-create chord —
`packages/herdr/src/shortcut-config.ts` / `loadShortcutConfig`, worklist input loop) that
set the focused work item's assignee to one of the two hold identities, or clear it.
The leader key is `o` (owner), keeping `a` reserved for the audit command family:

- `o p` — assignee = `producer` (persistent scheduling hold)
- `o a` — assignee = `agent` (session claim)
- `o n` — clear the assignee (`--assignee ""`, item becomes dispatchable)

The `a d` / `o d` dispatcher chord is **deferred** (see Appendix): the dispatcher identity's
non-hold semantics are not yet established, so no dispatcher chord ships in this work.

## Problem statement

The assignee/hold machine is opaque to operators working in herdr. They must hand-edit
via CLI to set scheduling holds (producer), tag agent claims, or clear stale holds — no
direct UI access.

## Goal

Give the operator one-key access to the scheduling-hold semantics that drive dispatch:
setting a producer hold, tagging an agent claim, or clearing a stale hold — without
hand-editing via CLI.

## Users

- **herdr operators** managing work-item dispatch and scheduling from the worklist view.
- **Downtime agents** that need to quickly set/clear holds during incident response.

### User stories

- *As a herdr operator*, I want to press `o p` on a work item to set a persistent producer
  hold, so that the downtime dispatcher respects the hold during scheduling.
- *As a herdr operator*, I want to press `o a` to tag an item with an agent claim, so
  I can signal ownership without creating a full worklog session.
- *As a herdr operator*, I want to press `o n` to clear a stale assignee, so items become
  dispatchable again without CLI editing.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1**: The three chords (`o p` / `o a` / `o n`) are registered in the herdr
  shortcut config for the worklist view and work on the focused item.
- **AC2**: Each chord runs `wl update <id> --assignee <value>` (or the equivalent
  worklog-dir-safe update) against the focused item; `o n` clears the assignee.
- **AC3**: The updates flow through the standard command/refresh path (a completion-refresh
  re-renders the worklist, mirroring chord-quick-create).
- **AC4**: Chord conflicts are handled: the leader key `o` and the second keys (`p`, `a`, `n`)
  must not collide with existing handlers (quit-key case documented in chord-quick-create;
  the `a` leader stays reserved for audit).
- **AC5**: The chords are documented in the herdr README keybinding reference, with
  the hold semantics of each identity (`producer` = persistent hold, `agent` = session claim,
  empty = dispatchable), and a note that a dispatcher chord is deferred until its
  non-hold semantics land.
- **AC6**: Unit tests drive the real worklist input loop with the production shortcut registry
  for all three chords (same harness as chord-quick-create.test.ts), asserting the dispatched
  `wl update` command and assignee value.
- **AC7**: Full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Impact

Operators gain direct worklist access to scheduling holds without leaving herdr or editing CLI.

## Constraints

- Must follow the existing `c q` quick-create chord pattern (same shortcut config mechanism,
  same worklist input loop integration).
- The `a` leader key remains reserved for the audit command family (`a a`/`a y`/`a r`).
- No dispatcher chord in this work — the dispatcher identity semantics are not yet
  established (deferred; see Appendix).
- Follow the settings/shortcut validation pattern in `packages/herdr/src/settings.ts`.
- Chords must be safe during Code Freeze (ship skill gates itself on `S`).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/shortcut-config.ts` — chord registry
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` / `worklist.state.ts` / `worklist.constants.ts` — input
  loop and focused-item resolution
- `packages/herdr/src/chord-quick-create.test.ts` — test harness to mirror
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — keybinding documentation

## Related work

- discovered-from: WL-0MVR8GDJ3008WY3Y — Downtime leader cannot see a worklog root with no
  running herdr instance (the stack that exposed how opaque the assignee/hold machine is).
- WL-0MW51OB1Y0073TLG — Dispatcher claims work items as 'dispatcher' instead of producer
  sentinel 'Map' (critical; defines the `dispatcher` identity — **deferred**, no chord ships here).
- WL-0MTCLB50D0026YA7 — the `c q` quick-create chord this work mirrors.

## Risks & Assumptions

| Risk | Mitigation |
|------|-----------|
| Chord collision with existing shortcuts | Follow chord-quick-create's conflict-detection pattern; `o` leader and `o a`/`o p`/`o n` second keys tested; `a` leader untouched |
| Scope creep: operators request more assignee values / dispatcher chord | Record as a linked follow-up; keep to the three documented chords; dispatcher chord deferred per producer |
| `o` conflicts with future chords | Document the `o` = owner-axis reservation in README and shortcuts.json descriptions |

**Assumptions:**
- The `wl update --assignee` path is stable and works from the herdr process context.
- Code Freeze does not need to block these chords (they mutate state, not ship).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Is `a a` collision acceptable? Should we pick a different chord for assignee=agent?"
  Answer (producer): "Keep `a` for the audit commands currently implemented and use `o` (owner)
  for these new commands." Final: leader key is `o`; `o p`/`o a`/`o n`.
- Q: "Should `a d` be gated/hidden until WL-0MW51OB1Y0073TLG is implemented? Or should we create
  a new work item to re-establish the dispatcher identity work?"
  Answer (producer): "Drop a-d for now." Final: no dispatcher chord ships in this work.
- Q: "Should the dispatcher identity semantics be defined in this work item, or remain a dependency?"
  Answer (producer): "n/a (see 2)". Final: no dispatcher work in this item.

# Regression guard: `wl update --audit-text` survives a drifted-but-repairable DB

discovered-from:AH-0MW4W2CAJ000NUJZ

## Context

The 2026-11-06 AI_Hell release run surfaced an audit-persistence failure: the
ship audit gate's `wl update --audit-text` exited rc=1 while the AI_Hell
worklog database was drifted (`schemaVersion=8` vs the installed tool's
`9`), so neither the assembled audit report nor the compact fallback notice
could be persisted. The current build heals such a database on connect
(`REQUIRED_COLUMNS` in `packages/shared/src/persistent-store.ts`), and a
unit-level repair test already exists
(`packages/shared/src/audit-fingerprint-repair.test.ts`, WL-0MUEBQLRD00288VV).
That test calls `saveAuditResult()` directly, so it does **not** prove the
production path — the `wl update --audit-text` **command** — still works
against a drifted database. A regression that broke the command (or bypassed
the store's repair) would leave that guard green.

## User story

As a release producer, I want a deterministic test that drives the real
`wl update --audit-text` command against a drifted-but-repairable worklog
database, so a future change cannot silently reintroduce the 2026-11-06
audit-persistence failure.

## Acceptance criteria

1. A test in the ContextHub `wl` suite (`tests/cli/update-audit-text-schema-drift.test.ts`)
   proves that `wl update --audit-text` succeeds (rc=0, `success: true`)
   against a temp-DB fixture drifted to `schemaVersion=8` with the
   `audit_results.fingerprint` column dropped and its
   `audit_fingerprint_added` metadata sentinel removed.
2. The test asserts the write actually landed: the `audit_results` row exists
   for the item with the expected summary and a non-null fingerprint, and the
   connect-time repair restored the `fingerprint` column plus its sentinel.
3. The test is deterministic and self-contained: temp directory
   (`createTempDir`/`enterTempDir` pattern), direct SQLite drift on that copy
   only, no live `wl`/`network`/`pi` calls.
4. A second test exercises the audit-skill persist sequence (`wl audit-set`
   then `wl update --audit-text`) against a drifted database and asserts both
   succeed, so the release-gate path end to end is covered.
5. The test fails against a build with the connect-time repair disabled and
   passes with it (red/green witness recorded on AH-0MW4W2CAJ000NUJZ).
6. `DOCTOR_AND_MIGRATIONS.md` documents that the connect-time repair keeps the
   audit-write command working on a drifted database and names the regression
   test that locks it in.
7. The full ContextHub `wl` suite passes.

## Constraints

- Test-only change plus documentation; no production behaviour change is
  intended. The connect-time repair is treated as intended drift-resilience
  (recorded assumption on AH-0MW4W2CAJ000NUJZ).
- Deterministic only: no live AI_Hell/ContextHub worklog mutation, no
  network, no `pi` invocation.
- Do not bump `CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION` or change migration semantics.

## Key Files

- `tests/cli/update-audit-text-schema-drift.test.ts` (new)
- `tests/cli/cli-helpers.ts` (helpers used as-is)
- `packages/shared/src/persistent-store.ts` (`REQUIRED_COLUMNS` behaviour under test)
- `src/commands/update.ts` (`--audit-text` write path)
- `src/commands/audit-result.ts` (`wl audit-set`)
- `DOCTOR_AND_MIGRATIONS.md` (docs)

## Related work

- AH-0MW4W2CAJ000NUJZ — parent tracker in AI_Hell (this item is its mirror)
- WL-0MUEBQLRD00288VV — additive schema repair + unit-level repair test
- WL-0MW1W61CG005K893 — migration fix basis (schemaVersion advance on zero pending)
- WL-0MW1VJKO3009MHE0 — ContextHub root `wl doctor upgrade --confirm` execution item

## Impact

Release producers can now be confident that `wl update --audit-text` keeps working on a drifted-but-repairable worklog database: the regression suite drives the real command and proves (red/green) that the connect-time repair is what keeps the audit write alive, so the 2026-11-06 audit-persistence failure cannot silently return.

# Herdr session-path round-trip tests fail under a hyphenated TMPDIR

## Problem statement

Two tests in `packages/herdr/src/index.test.ts` fail whenever the ambient
`TMPDIR` contains a hyphen:

- `worklogRootFromPiSessionPath decodes a pi session dir back to the worklog root`
- `defaultStalledPaneRootResolver falls back to the pi session path when cwd is absent`

Both build their fixture root with `mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), 'stallroot'))`
and then encode it the way Pi encodes a session directory (every `/` replaced
by `-`) before asserting that `worklogRootFromPiSessionPath` decodes it back.
The encoding is **lossy for any hyphen** in the path, so the assertion can only
hold when the whole root is hyphen-free — the test comment even says so
("Hyphen-free prefix so the pi session-path encoding ... round-trips
unambiguously"), but the *prefix* is hyphen-free while `tmpdir()` is not.

The test skill's runner now injects a disk-backed `TMPDIR`
(`/var/tmp/pi-test-<uid>`, SA-0MW3ENF32006BGN1) — hyphenated by construction —
so both tests fail on every agent-driven run:

```
x worklogRootFromPiSessionPath decodes a pi session dir back to the worklog root
  expected undefined to be '/var/tmp/pi-test-1000/stallroothPRXF4'
x defaultStalledPaneRootResolver falls back to the pi session path when cwd is absent
  expected null to be '/var/tmp/pi-test-1000/stallrootiznmd1'
```

## Impact

`packages/herdr/**` is a declared changed-scope test group, so any change that
touches herdr selects `npm --silent test -- packages/herdr/src` as the
implement-finish gate — which is now red for an unrelated, environment-only
reason. Workaround in use: `PI_TEST_TMPDIR=/tmp/<hyphen-free>`. The dev-push
pre-push gate (`npm --silent test -- tests`) does not include this group, so a
push is not blocked, but the changed-scope gate is.

Reproduced on `dev` at 4d105bf8 with no local changes, both in the main
checkout and in a linked worktree: 2 failed tests; green with
`PI_TEST_TMPDIR=/tmp/pitestwork`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `packages/herdr/src/index.test.ts` no longer depends on `tmpdir()` being
      hyphen-free: the round-trip assertions pass under a hyphenated
      `TMPDIR` (e.g. `TMPDIR=/var/tmp/pi-test-1000`) as well as a hyphen-free one.
- [ ] The test keeps asserting the real decode contract for a hyphen-free root
      (no silent `skip` that removes the coverage on the machines that run it).
- [ ] `npm --silent test -- packages/herdr/src` is green under the test skill's
      default disk-backed `TMPDIR` (no `PI_TEST_TMPDIR` override).
- [ ] Record which side owns the durable fix (this repo's test fixture vs the
      test skill's `pi-test-<uid>` TMPDIR naming, SorraAgents) and link the
      companion item if one is needed.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/index.test.ts` — `makeRoot()` and the two session-path
  round-trip assertions (stalled-work production wiring block).

## Related work

- `discovered-from:WL-0MVVLBTTP003Y4XO` — the hyphenated-TMPDIR failures were
  found while running that item's changed-scope gate.
- WL-0MUYMBSA90092QV2 — introduced the stalled-work production wiring (and these
  two tests).

# Dispatcher opening a pane but not executing a command

**Headline:** The dispatcher provisions a work item's item-ID tab (and its empty placeholder root pane) *before* the host-budget admission gate; when the implement or audit tier is at its machine-wide cap the dispatch is refused before the spawn, so the placeholder pane is orphaned — an empty pane appears in a fresh item tab with no command ever run.

## Problem statement

A dispatch can open a pane without ever running its command. Both dispatch channels create the destination item-ID tab (herdr's empty root pane) *before* the dispatch is admitted, but the root-pane cleanup only runs *after a confirmed spawn*. When host-budget admission refuses the tick — the audit tier is at `maxAudit` or the implement tier is at `maxImplement` — the code returns before the spawn and the freshly created placeholder pane is left behind.

Live evidence collected on 2026-11-06:

- `w3G:p1BK` — empty bash pane in tab `MS-0MW3LTMHT001PRDT` (workspace `w3G`, cwd `tce-main-street`), no label, no agent, no command.
- `w57:pCV` — empty bash pane in tab `SA-0MVXUGXS5006M3HF` (workspace `w57`, cwd `ContextHub/packages/herdr`), no label, no agent, no command.
- Both work items are `completed / in_review`, i.e. **audit** candidates, which matches the audit-tier refusal below.
- The machine ledger `/home/rgardler/.herdr/downtime/dispatch-budget.json` held **2 implement** entries (both live panes `w3G:p1BB`, `w3G:p1BG` ⇒ at the default `maxImplement: 2`) and **1 audit** entry for `MS-0MW1ZSC7U000V5MW` whose pane `w3G:p1B9` no longer exists. With no `budget.json`, caps fall back to the defaults, so both budgeted tiers refused while the placeholder panes were already on screen.

The orphaned pane is therefore a *presentation* defect triggered by a legitimate budget refusal: the budget stop itself is correct; leaving the empty pane is not. The stale audit ledger entry that triggers the refusal is filed separately as `discovered-from:WL-0MW5KC8J300942EA` so this item stays focused on the pane lifecycle.

## Users

- **Operator / producer.** As the herdr operator, I want a refused dispatch to leave *no* trace pane, so I never have to distinguish an empty leftover tab from a dispatch that is genuinely starting.
- **Downtime dispatcher.** As the dispatch admission path, I want the destination tab provisioned only once the dispatch is admitted (or cleaned up on abort), so a budget stop, claim loss, reservation refusal or spawn failure cannot leak a pane.
- **Campaign / worktree owner.** As the owner of a project workspace, I want no empty tabs accumulating under my work-item IDs when dispatch is saturated.

Example user stories:

- "When the audit cap is reached, I see the budget notice and *no* new empty pane in the item's tab."
- "When I cancel the host-budget dialog on a manual implement, the item tab I just caused to be created is not left empty."
- "When every gate passes and only the spawn fails, the placeholder pane is closed rather than orphaned."

## Existing state

Two independent ordering sites both provision the item-ID tab before the gate that can refuse the dispatch:

1. **Downtime dispatcher** — `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.dispatch-claims.ts` (`dispatchClaimedTier`) runs, in order: resolve/provision the item-ID tab anchor (`deps.resolveProjectWorkspace` → `deps.getItemTabAnchor`), CAS claim (`deps.claimItem`), local-capacity reservation, **host-budget admission** (`deps.admitHostDispatch`), marker write, spawn. The root-pane cleanup (`anchorIsTabRoot` → `deps.closePane`) sits *after* a successful spawn, so a host-budget refusal (`host-budget-implement` / `host-budget-audit` / `host-budget-unknown`) leaves the placeholder pane.
2. **Interactive / manual dispatch** — `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` (`onCommand`, route `agent`) calls `resolveInteractiveItemAnchor` (which provisions the tab) *before* `prepareInteractiveAgentDispatch` (the host-budget gate). A budget-cancel returns without any spawn, and the `createdItemTabAnchor` cleanup only runs after a confirmed split.

Prior, adjacent fixes did not cover the abort path:

- **WL-0MUYI3K8H007MPKF** — interactive item-tab root-pane cleanup, explicitly scoped to *after a pane spawns*.
- **WL-0MU2EOHK900425VU** — dispatcher workspace "useless pane" and the downtime path's post-spawn cleanup.

Both stop short of "the dispatch never spawned".

## Desired change

- Provision the item-ID tab only once the dispatch is admitted, so a refusal cannot create a pane in the first place.
  - Downtime path: move the item-tab anchor provisioning to after host-budget admission (and after the reservation gate), immediately before the marker write, while preserving the F3 contract that admission happens after the CAS claim and before the marker/spawn.
  - Interactive path: resolve/provision the item anchor only after `prepareInteractiveAgentDispatch` has decided to proceed.
- As defence in depth, run the existing fail-safe root-pane cleanup on **every** pre-spawn abort path that did provision a tab (claim lost/failed, reservation refusal, TTL-below-bound above the usable window, host-budget refusal, marker-write failure, spawn failure, interactive budget-cancel).
- Keep the cleanup fail-safe: only close a placeholder root pane when liveness positively confirms it is not a live tracked pane; never close a reused tab's live anchor.

## Constraints

- The budget gate's semantics and contract must not weaken: admission still happens once, after the CAS claim and before the marker/spawn (F3 AC3, WL-0MVXY0YG7009JMHI).
- Cleanup is best-effort and fail-open: a cleanup failure never changes the dispatch outcome, never throws, and never turns a neutral refusal into a strike.
- Reuse the existing anchor/liveness/close primitives (`resolveProjectWorkspace`, `getItemTabAnchor`, `resolveInteractiveItemAnchor`, `closePane`, `getRunningDowntimePanes`, `closeInteractiveTabRootPane`); do not invent a new pane/tab mechanism.
- Never close a live pane: the liveness check must fail safe (unknown ⇒ leave open).
- Do not attempt to fix the stale audit ledger entry here — that is `discovered-from:WL-0MW5KC8J300942EA`.
- Agent-initiated test runs go through the test skill; the pre-push hook and `implement.py finish` are infrastructure and out of scope of that rule.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.dispatch-claims.ts` — reorder item-tab provisioning relative to host-budget admission; invoke the root-pane cleanup on every pre-spawn abort that provisioned a tab.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — interactive `onCommand`: move `resolveInteractiveItemAnchor` after the budget gate proceeds, and clean up `createdItemTabAnchor` on the cancel/abort path.
- `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.ts` — `getItemTabAnchor` / `resolveInteractiveItemAnchor` provisioning seams and the created-vs-reused signal.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.pane.ts` — `closePane` / running-pane liveness conventions reused by the cleanup.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.dispatch*.test.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/*anchor*.test.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/host-dispatch-budget.*.test.ts` — regression coverage for the refusal-before-provision and abort-cleanup paths.
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — document the ordering (admission before provisioning) and the no-orphan-pane guarantee.

## Acceptance criteria

- A dispatch refused by host-budget admission (implement or audit, either dispatcher path) leaves **no** orphaned pane: either the item-ID placeholder is never created, or it is closed before the tick returns.
- Every other pre-spawn abort in `dispatchClaimedTier` (claim lost/failed, local-capacity reservation refusal, TTL-below-bound, marker-write failure, spawn failure) leaves **no** orphaned placeholder pane that the dispatch itself created.
- An interactive agent dispatch cancelled at the host-budget dialog leaves **no** orphaned placeholder pane in the item tab it provisioned.
- Existing fail-safe cleanup is preserved: a reused item tab whose anchor hosts a live tracked pane is never closed, and unavailable liveness leaves the anchor open.
- Regression tests cover, at minimum, (a) budget refusal creates no pane / closes the placeholder, (b) each pre-spawn abort path leaves no orphan, and (c) the reused-live-anchor and unknown-liveness fail-safe cases; the tests fail against the current ordering.
- The ordering and the no-orphan-pane guarantee are documented in `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope creep:** the budget ledger lifecycle (stale entries, reaping) will tempt a combined fix; kept out of scope via `discovered-from:WL-0MW5KC8J300942EA`.
- **Ordering change risk:** moving provisioning after admission means an `anchor-unavailable` (or a thrown resolver) now occurs *after* the CAS claim, so the claim must be rolled back on that failure exactly as the existing abort paths do. Preserve the rollback invariants.
- **Reused-tab risk:** a "cleanup on abort" that ignores the created-vs-reused signal could close a live anchor on a reused tab; the fail-safe liveness gate and the created-signal must both hold.
- **Assumption:** the host-budget refusal genuinely happens before the spawn on both paths (confirmed by reading `dispatchClaimedTier` and `onCommand`); the orphaned evidence panes correspond to the item tabs created by those refusals.
- **Assumption:** the budget being at cap is correct behaviour (two live implement panes; one fresh audit entry). Only the leftover pane is a defect here.

## Related work

- `discovered-from:WL-0MW5KC8J300942EA` — *Stale audit dispatch-budget ledger entry survives its closed pane and holds the audit tier at cap* (the current trigger of the refusal).
- **Implement: interactive item-tab root-pane cleanup** (WL-0MUYI3K8H007MPKF) — post-spawn cleanup this item extends to the abort path.
- **dispatcher workspace has useless pane** (WL-0MU2EOHK900425VU) — the downtime path's post-spawn root-pane cleanup.
- **Implement: interactive item-tab placement (both channels)** (WL-0MUYI3JAO002BTNL) and parent **WL-0MUKZGEQ2007FECS** — the placement mechanism whose placeholder pane is leaked.
- **F3 — Implement-tier admission on both dispatcher paths** (WL-0MVXY0YG7009JMHI) — the host-budget admission whose placement relative to provisioning is the root cause.
- **F2 — Audit tier 1→N generalisation and active-audit unification** (WL-0MVXY0XPF006YUHA).
- **Generalise host dispatch budget to any work item type** (WL-0MW50EHZ6007QBPB) — open; widens which tiers can refuse, so the no-orphan guarantee must hold for every kind.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

Recorded from the interactive intake interview (producer replies, this session).

- **Q1 — Which dispatch channels are in scope?** (a) both the automatic downtime dispatcher and manual/interactive dispatch; (b) only the automatic dispatcher; (c) only manual/interactive. — **Answer (producer):** "continue" = accept the recommended option **(a) both channels**. Rationale: both share the same provision-before-gate ordering and both leaked a placeholder pane in the evidence. Source: interactive reply, 2026-11-06.
- **Q2 — Is the stale audit ledger entry in scope?** (a) separate `discovered-from` item, keep this item focused on the orphaned pane; (b) fold the stale-entry release into this item; (c) fold the stale entry and a broader budget-lifecycle audit in. — **Answer (producer):** "continue" = accept the recommended option **(a) separate `discovered-from` item**. Filed as **WL-0MW5KC8J300942EA**. Source: interactive reply, 2026-11-06.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MUYI3K8H007MPKF** – Implement: interactive item-tab root-pane cleanup (completed)
- **WL-0MW50EHZ6007QBPB** – Generalise host dispatch budget to any work item type (absent = unlimited, audit-only over-hold) (open)
- **WL-0MW5E5V20002T0KW** – Implement left-of-extensions tab placement for interactive dispatches (blocked)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — matched: 0mu2eohk900425vu, 0mukzgeq2007fecs, 0muyi3jao002btnl, 0muyi3k8h007mpkf, 0mvxy0xpf006yuha (+332 more)
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — matched: 0mukzgeq2007fecs, 0muyi3jao002btnl, 0mvxy0xpf006yuha, abort, ac3 (+312 more)
- `CLI.md` — matched: abort, accept, active, agent, already (+249 more)

## Impact

A dispatch that is refused or aborts before spawning leaves no empty placeholder pane in the work item's tab — operators no longer have to tell a leftover blank pane from a dispatch that is genuinely starting.

discovered-from:WL-0MW5JE0SZ0057K30.

## Problem

The machine-scoped dispatch-budget ledger (`/home/rgardler/.herdr/downtime/dispatch-budget.json`, `packages/herdr/src/host-dispatch-budget.ts`) is holding an **audit** entry for `MS-0MW1ZSC7U000V5MW` (pane `w3G:p1B9`, heartbeat `2026-11-06T21:02:53Z`) whose pane no longer exists in `herdr pane list`. Because the audit tier counts fresh entries without a live-pane requirement (`freshCount`), the dead entry keeps the audit tier at its default `maxAudit: 1` cap until the 2 h staleness window expires.

## Incident evidence

Observed on 2026-11-06 while investigating WL-0MW5JE0SZ0057K30: the audit tier refused every `completed/in_review` candidate (`MS-0MW3LTMHT001PRDT`, `SA-0MVXUGXS5006M3HF`) for ~90 minutes after their audit pane had closed.

## Impact

Audit dispatch recovers as soon as an audit pane closes — the tier stops reporting a phantom in-progress audit and admits the next `completed/in_review` candidate immediately instead of stalling for up to two hours.

## Desired change

Release or reap an audit ledger entry when its pane closes (the `recordPaneClose` best-effort release is not firing on every close path), so a closed audit pane does not hold the audit cap for the remainder of the staleness window.

## Notes

- Distinct from WL-0MW5JE0SZ0057K30, which fixes the orphaned item-tab placeholder pane left when the budget refuses a dispatch.
- Related: WL-0MVXY0XPF006YUHA (audit tier / active-audit unification), WL-0MVXY0YG7009JMHI (implement-tier admission), WL-0MW50EHZ6007QBPB (generalise the budget).

## Acceptance Criteria

- A machine-ledger entry with a non-empty \`paneId\` that is absent from a trusted machine-wide live pane list is removed on the next pane-close-reaper pass regardless of heartbeat freshness, so a closed audit pane cannot hold \`maxAudit\` for the remainder of the 2 h staleness window.
- The pane-close reaper releases the item's host-dispatch ledger entry immediately after it closes that pane (implement and audit kinds), idempotently.
- Unconfirmed entries (no \`paneId\`, the reserve→spawn window) and entries whose pane is live are retained; no sweep is applied when the live pane list cannot be read (fail-safe: no over-reaping, no over-admission).
- Regression coverage: unit tests for the ledger sweep (dead / live / unconfirmed / stale), the reaper's post-close release and ledger-sweep seams (success, dry-run, failed close, throwing seam), and the \`createHerdrReaperDeps\` wiring.
- \`docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md\` documents the ledger release points and the dead-pane sweep.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Key Files (predicted)

- \`packages/herdr/src/host-dispatch-budget.ts\` — new \`sweepClosedPanes\` (drop confirmed entries whose pane is absent, plus stale entries).
- \`packages/herdr/src/host-dispatch-budget.test.ts\` — sweep unit tests.
- \`packages/herdr/src/pane-close-reaper.ts\` — \`ReaperDeps.releasePaneBudget\` + \`sweepBudgetLedger\` seams; call after a successful close and after listing panes.
- \`packages/herdr/src/pane-close-reaper.test.ts\` — reaper seam tests.
- \`packages/herdr/src/pane-close-herdr.ts\` — \`HerdrReaperIo\` seams + passthrough in \`createHerdrReaperDeps\`.
- \`packages/herdr/src/index.ts\` — wire the seams to \`releaseHostDispatch\` / \`sweepClosedPanes\`; \`readAuditBudgetState\` liveness refinement if needed.
- \`packages/herdr/src/pane-close-cli.ts\` — wire the CLI reaper seams.
- \`docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md\`.

# Intake Draft — Add parent field to concise format of wl show output (WL-0MW5M5GUF0051D4N)

## Problem statement

The concise format of `wl show` (`-F concise`) omits the parent relationship entirely: an item with a parent shows no indication of it, so a user must switch to `normal` or `full` format to see which parent item a work item belongs to. The `normal` and `full` formats both already render a conditional `Parent` row; the `concise` format should do the same.

## Users

- **Primary**: Developers and operators using `wl show -F concise` (and `wl list -F concise`, which reuses the same formatter) to inspect work items compactly.
  - User story: As a user viewing a work item in concise format, I want to see its parent ID so I can trace the item's position in the work hierarchy without switching format.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `wl show <id> -F concise` renders a `Parent` row in the metadata table when the item has a `parentId` set, displaying the parent's ID. The row sits after `Effort` and before `Assignee`, matching the `normal`/`full` row order.
2. When the item has no parent, no `Parent` row appears in concise output (the row is conditional on `parentId` being set).
3. The `Parent` row renders correctly in both plain-text and markdown/TTY rendering of the concise format.
4. `wl list -F concise` tree rendering reflects the same change without regressing tree output (it delegates to the same formatter).
5. A unit test asserts the `Parent` row appears in concise output when `parentId` is set and is absent when it is not; all existing tests pass with the change.
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

Users of `wl show -F concise` can now see an item's parent at a glance, instead of switching to normal/full output to trace the hierarchy.

## Constraints

- **No changes** to `summary`, `raw`, `--fields` projected output, `normal`, or `full` formats.
- The `Parent` row is conditional on `parentId` being truthy — never a placeholder row in concise mode.
- Preserve the existing concise row order; insert `Parent` after `Effort`, before `Assignee`, consistent with `normal`/`full`.

## Existing state

- `src/commands/helpers.ts` → `humanFormatWorkItem()`: both `full` and `normal` format blocks already include `if (item.parentId) metaRows.push(['Parent', item.parentId]);`.
- The `concise` block (in the same function) builds its metadata table with: `Status` (incl. Stage | Priority), `SortIndex`, `Risk`, `Effort`, then conditional `Assignee`, `Audit`, `Tags` — no `Parent` row.
- Concise format is used by `wl show -F concise` and reused by the tree renderer `displayItemTreeWithFormat(items, db, 'concise')` for `wl list -F concise`.

## Desired change

- Add `if (item.parentId) metaRows.push(['Parent', item.parentId]);` to the `concise` block of `humanFormatWorkItem()` in `src/commands/helpers.ts`, after the `Effort` row.

## Key Files

- `src/commands/helpers.ts` — Add the conditional `Parent` row to the concise block of `humanFormatWorkItem()`.
- `tests/cli/helpers-tree-rendering.test.ts` — Logically adjacent concise-format tests (Risk/Effort rows); candidate home for the new coverage.
- `tests/unit/human-audit-format.test.ts` — Snapshot tests of concise/normal/full; items have no `parentId`, so unaffected, but adjacent precedent.
- `tests/integration/wl-show-formatting.test.ts` — Formatting integration tests (mock item has `parentId: null`; unaffected).
- `CLI.md` — `-F concise` documented only by examples; verify no row-by-row description needs updating.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption**: the `if (item.parentId)` truthiness guard matches `normal`/`full` behaviour (an empty string is treated as "no parent").
- **Assumption**: snapshot tests in `tests/unit/human-audit-format.test.ts` and `tests/cli/human-show-list-audit-snapshots.test.ts` use items without a parent, so no snapshot churn is expected; verify on run.

# Ship opens in own tab (WL-0MW6FIZYI0003QEU)

**Headline**: The Ship It shortcut (`S`) dispatches the dev→main release (`/skill:ship release`) into a pi pane that currently splits the **current tab**. Change it so the release runs in **its own tab labelled `Ship`** in the invoking workspace — created on first use, reused thereafter, focused on open, placed left of the extensions/Work Items tab — and reject a second Ship command while the first release is still active.

## Problem statement

When an operator presses `S` in the herdr worklist selection list and confirms with `ship` + Enter, the release pi pane opens by splitting the current pane/tab, scattering the release in whatever tab the operator happened to be in. Ship is already a distinct, guarded workflow (typed-confirmation dialog, ship guard, code-freeze marker), so its pane should live in a dedicated, recognisable `Ship` tab — and a second release must not be started while the first is still running.

## Users

- **Herdr operator running a dev→main release**:
  > "As an operator, when I press `S` and confirm `ship`, I want the release pi session to open in a tab titled **Ship** so I can find it immediately and keep the release runner separate from the selection list and other work-tabs."
- **Operator running repeated releases**:
  > "As an operator who ships several times a day, I want the Ship tab to be reused (one release per tab) and a second Ship command rejected while a release is still active, so I never accidentally start two releases or clutter the tab row."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Ship dispatch opens in its own tab** — pressing `S` and confirming with `ship` + Enter dispatches `/skill:ship release` into a tab labelled exactly `Ship` in the invoking pane's current workspace (created on first use, reused thereafter) instead of splitting the current pane/tab. Verified via `herdr tab list --workspace <ws>` (`label == 'Ship'`) and the spawned pi pane's `tab_id` matching that tab.
2. **Second Ship while active is rejected** — while the first release is still active (its Ship pane is live), a second `S` → confirm does **not** dispatch: a blocked notice is shown (no dialog/confirm opens), mirroring the existing ship-guard behaviour. No second pi pane is spawned.
3. **Focus the Ship pane** — the release pi pane is focused/zoomed on open so the operator immediately sees the release run (the pane may still be focused without stealing list focus, consistent with `focus: true` shortcut behaviour).
4. **Fresh Ship tab placed left-of-extensions** — a newly created `Ship` tab is placed immediately left of the extensions/Work Items tab (`'left-of-extensions'`), matching interactive item-ID tab placement; a reused tab is never repositioned.
5. **Fail-open placement** — if the `Ship` tab cannot be resolved or created (CLI failure, no workspace, guard query failure), the dispatch falls back to the current-pane split exactly as today — the release is never blocked by tab provisioning.
6. **Testing/validation** — unit + TUI integration tests cover: the Ship pane lands in the `Ship` tab (anchor pane id forwarded to `send-to-pi.sh`); the rejected second-command path; focus forwarding; left-of-extensions placement of a fresh tab; and the fail-open fallback.
7. **All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant docs-site or wiki entries (e.g. the ship-it dialog / placement docs).
8. **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Impact

Operators can now start a dev→main release from the worklist and watch it run in a dedicated, always-findable `Ship` tab — with a fresh tab placed beside the work items and a second release safely rejected while the first is still running.

## Constraints

- Reuse the existing interactive tab machinery (`getItemTabAnchor` / `resolveInteractiveItemAnchor`, `herdr tab create --workspace <id> --label <label> --no-focus`) — do not introduce a parallel tab-provisioning path.
- The typed ship confirmation dialog (WL-0MSGG5N5Z0074TLY), ship guard (WL-0MUD6DDZC007ZSIW) and code-freeze marker flow stay intact; this item changes only *where* the dispatch pane lands and adds the second-command rejection.
- Global release command: `/skill:ship release` carries **no work-item ID**, so today `interactiveItemId` is `undefined` and the interactive item-ID anchor path returns `null`. The `Ship` label must be substituted for the missing item ID on this path only.
- Focus is currently *not* passed for the ship dispatch (`--no-focus`); this item adds focus explicitly.
- No push to `main`; work is committed to `dev` per the push policy.

## Existing state

- `packages/herdr/src/shortcuts.json` — `S` → `/skill:ship release` (view `both`).
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — `openShipItDialogGuarded`/`openShipItDialog`; on confirm, `executeResolvedCommand(SHIP_IT_COMMAND, state, opts.onCommand, frozen, model, opts.onDowntimeToggle, undefined, opts.onRefresh)`; `dispatchChordCommand` routes `/skill:ship` → `resolveAndRouteCommand` → `onCommand(command, model, ...)` (paneTitle = selected item's title, focus undefined).
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — `onCommand` agent route: `interactiveItemId = extractWorkItemId(command)` → `undefined` for ship → `resolveInteractiveItemAnchorAfterAdmission` returns `null` → `--anchor` omitted → `send-to-pi.sh` splits the current pane (current tab).
- `packages/herdr/src/index.interactive.ts` — `resolveInteractiveItemAnchor(cwd, workspaceId, itemId, ...)` wraps `getItemTabAnchor`; fails open to `null` (current-pane split) on any error; supports `'left-of-extensions'` placement.
- `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.placement.ts` — `getItemTabAnchor` creates-or-reuses a tab whose label is the key.
- `packages/herdr/src/ship-guard.ts` — `runShipGuard`/`formatBlockedNotice` gate ship entry on live panes carrying project work-item IDs (blocked-notice UI already exists to reuse for the second-command rejection).

## Desired change

1. In the interactive agent dispatch path (`index.ts` `onCommand`), when the resolved command is `SHIP_IT_COMMAND` (`/skill:ship release`), resolve the interactive tab anchor with the literal label **`Ship`** instead of the (missing) work-item ID — reusing `resolveInteractiveItemAnchor`/`getItemTabAnchor` so the tab is created on first use and reused thereafter. Forward the anchor's pane id to `send-to-pi.sh` via `--anchor`, producing a pi pane inside the `Ship` tab.
2. Use `'left-of-extensions'` placement for a freshly created `Ship` tab (a reused tab is never moved).
3. Pass `focus: true` on the ship dispatch so the release pane is focused/zoomed on open.
4. Extend the ship-entry gate so a second Ship command is rejected while the first release is active: the guard (or a lightweight check on the same `shipGuardQuery` pane data) treats a live pane in the `Ship` tab as blocking — show the existing blocked notice, never open the confirmation dialog.
5. Fail-open: any anchor resolution/creation failure keeps today's current-pane split.

## Key Files:

- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — the `onCommand` agent route: substitute the `Ship` label for the item-ID anchor lookup, forward `--anchor` + `--focus`.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.interactive.ts` — `resolveInteractiveItemAnchor` (reused; may need a label param or ship-specific caller).
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — ship dialog dispatch (`openShipItDialog.*`, `executeResolvedCommand` call), second-command rejection gate wiring, `SHIP_IT_COMMAND` handling.
- `packages/herdr/src/ship-guard.ts` — extend guard result to include a live `Ship`-tab pane as a blocking condition (rejection path).
- `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.placement.ts` / `.herdr-cli.ts` — existing `getItemTabAnchor` / `createTabInWorkspace` reused unchanged.
- `packages/herdr/src/shortcuts.json` — `S` shortcut entry (unchanged unless focus/code_freeze policy changes).
- Tests: `packages/herdr/src/ship-it-dialog-tui.test.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/ship-guard-tui.test.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/index.interactive.test.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/ship-guard.test.ts`.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Title/requirement wording**: the item title says "own pane" but the requirement (and operator's confirmation) is an own *tab* labelled `Ship`; the pane inside the tab is the pi session. Implementation should key on the tab, not a pane rename.
- **Second-command rejection signal**: "first release still active" is interpreted as *a live pi pane in the `Ship` tab* (from the same `shipGuardQuery` pane list). If pane-liveness cannot be determined (query failure), fail safe the same way the existing guard does (blocked notice) — never open a second release.
- **Scope creep**: embedding extra capacity work in this item is out of scope — record as linked work items if discovered (e.g. a "reuse completed Ship tab" toggle, per-workspace Ship tabs, pane renaming policy).
- **Assumption**: placement, focus and rejection apply to the interactive `S` shortcut dispatch path only; other `/skill:ship` invocations keep current behaviour unless the same code path is shared.

## Related work

- WL-0MSGG5N5Z0074TLY — Ship It shortcut + typed confirmation dialog (parent requirement: dispatch path).
- WL-0MUD6DDZC007ZSIW — code freeze on ship confirmation + ship guard semantics (extension point for the second-command rejection).
- WL-0MUKZGEQ2007FECS — Pi processes start in a work-item tab (the item-ID tab machinery this item reuses with a fixed `Ship` label).
- WL-0MVZ88G51004IYHW / WL-0MW5E5V20002T0KW — left-of-extensions tab placement (fresh-tab placement policy).
- WL-0MUDEGBGO00609RV — ship-guard pure module (guard extension point).

## Related work (automated report)

- **WL-0ML5YRMB11GQV4HR** – Slash Command Palette (completed)
- **WL-0MSG6ZI3D003VYZZ** – Fix resize-mode anchor resolution: herdr pane current rejects --json (completed)
- **WL-0MTR2HLLJ009PTPJ** – Wire pane spawn to use persisted dispatcher anchor (completed)

### Repository file matches

- `CLI.md`
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`
- `packages/herdr/README.md`

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Tab lifecycle — should a second Ship command reuse an existing 'Ship' tab, or always open a fresh tab?" — Answer (operator): "A second ship command while the first is still active should be rejected." — Source: interactive reply. Interpretation: one release at a time — the `Ship` tab is created on first use and reused, and a second Ship command while the first release is active is blocked (never a fresh tab, never a second pane in the same tab). Prior options offered/rejected: reuse the tab (preferred at the time) vs fresh tab each time (rejected — would allow concurrent releases).
- Q2: "Where should a freshly created 'Ship' tab be placed?" — Answer (operator): **A — left-of-extensions** (same placement as interactive item-ID tabs, WL-0MW5E5V20002T0KW). Source: interactive reply.
- Q3: "Should the Ship pane take focus when it opens?" — Answer (operator): **B — focus the Ship pane** so the operator immediately sees the release run. Source: interactive reply. Note: current behaviour is `--no-focus`; this item changes it for the Ship dispatch only.

## Problem statement

The herdr selection list `r-p` (Producer Review) shortcut runs `!!wl reviewed <id> && wl comment add <id> --body '<producer_comment>' --author <author>`. It does not declare `open_pane: false`, so after the operator enters the producer comment, a command-output pane opens to display the output — even though the command has no meaningful output to show. The `open_pane: false` mechanism is already established (WL-0MSJLD1I70045ZUL) and the command has no placeholders, so the fix is a single-property addition to the shortcut config.

## Users

- **Producers / reviewers** using `r-p` to toggle the 'Needs Producer Review' flag on work items. They expect a quiet, non-intrusive action — entering a comment and pressing enter should just work, without opening a pointless command pane.
  - *As a producer, I want to mark items for review and add a comment without being forced to dismiss a command-output pane.*

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **No pane for `r-p`** — Pressing `r-p` on a selected work item, entering a producer comment, and submitting results in **no herdr pane being opened**; the command runs in the background with stdout/stderr captured to a log file.
2. **Default behaviour unchanged** — Shortcuts without `open_pane: false` still open a pane as before (no regression).

5. **All related documentation is updated** to reflect the change, including code comments and `packages/herdr/README.md`.

## Impact

Producers can mark items for review and add comments without having to dismiss a pointless command-output pane after every use.

## Constraints

- **Single-property change** — only add `open_pane: false` to the `r-p` shortcut entry in `shortcuts.json`; no code changes required.
- **Backward compatibility** — no behavioural changes for other shortcuts.

## Existing state

# Inconsistent soft-delete predicate: `wl list` excludes only `status=deleted` while `wl update` rejects any non-empty `deletedBy`

## Problem statement

Two code paths disagree about what counts as "soft-deleted":

- **`wl list`** excludes a row only when `status === 'deleted'` (`src/commands/list.ts`, the `includeDeleted` filter). It ignores `deletedBy`.
- **`wl update`** refuses to mutate a row whenever `deletedBy` is non-empty, regardless of `status` (`src/commands/update.ts`, the soft-delete guard `SA-0MUJBLZC60085DI9 AC1`, error code `deleted-item`). It ignores `status`.

The result is a row that is *both* visible and immutable:

- **visible** in `wl list --stage <X>` because its `status` is not `'deleted'`, and
- **immutable** because its `deletedBy` is set, so `wl update` rejects it as `deleted-item`.

## Problem impact

A soft-deleted-then-repaired item (e.g. `status=completed` with `deletedBy` retained to preserve deletion intent) that also carries `stage=in_review` shows up as a **release candidate** for `wl list --stage in_review`, but the audit runner's `wl update --status in_progress` fails with `deleted-item`. This blocks the `dev -> main` release gate (ship skill) for a row that is, by the CLI's own definition, deleted. It surfaced during the ship release attempt on 2026-11-06 (see MS-0MW22TQS8008021W), where four items had to be hand-repaired to clear `in_review` from the candidate list.

## Root cause

The two predicates are not derived from one shared definition of "soft-deleted":

| Path | Predicate | File / symbol |
|------|-----------|---------------|
| list | `item.status !== 'deleted'` | `src/commands/list.ts` — `includeDeleted` filter |
| update | `String(item.deletedBy ?? '').trim() !== ''` | `src/commands/update.ts` — soft-delete guard |

## Reproduction

1. Take a work item with `status=completed`, `stage=in_review`, and a non-empty `deletedBy` (e.g. any item repaired after a `wl delete`).
2. `wl list --stage in_review --json` → the item is returned as a candidate.
3. `wl update <id> --status in_progress --json` → `{ "success": false, "error": "deleted-item" }`.

Live evidence (tce-main-street store, 2026-11-08): the four items repaired during the ship run all have `status=completed`, `deletedBy=250240+SorraTheOrc@users.noreply.github.com`, `stage=done`:

- `wl list --stage done --json` returns all four.
- `wl update MS-0MT3JK16W006A66P --title probe --json` returns `success:false, error:"deleted-item"`.

If their `stage` had remained `in_review`, they would have blocked the release gate exactly as described in the ship comment.

## Desired change

Define "soft-deleted" once and use it consistently. Either:

- **Option A (preferred):** treat a row as excluded/deleted whenever `status === 'deleted'` **or** `deletedBy` is non-empty, in `wl list` (and any other read path that projects "live" items). This makes visible rows always mutable.
- **Option B:** have the `wl update` soft-delete guard key on `status === 'deleted'` only, and treat `deletedBy` as pure attribution for non-deleted rows.

The chosen option must be applied to **every** read/selection path that can feed the release gate (`wl list --stage`, `wl worklist`, `wl next`), not just `wl list`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1: A single shared predicate function defines "soft-deleted" for both read and write paths.
- [ ] AC2: A row with non-empty `deletedBy` is either excluded from every list/selection path **or** is mutable via `wl update` — the two paths must agree (no visible-but-immutable rows).
- [ ] AC3: Regression test: an item with `status !== 'deleted'` but non-empty `deletedBy` has consistent treatment — if it is returned by `wl list --stage in_review`, `wl update` must accept a mutation on it; if it is excluded, `wl list` must not return it.
- [ ] AC4: Regression test: `wl list --stage in_review` never returns a row the release gate cannot audit (i.e. never a row for which `wl update --status in_progress` fails with `deleted-item`).
- [ ] AC5: `wl doctor` reports no findings introduced by the change; existing soft-deleted rows remain excluded from normal lists.

## Key Files

- `src/commands/list.ts` — `includeDeleted` filter (list-side predicate).
- `src/commands/update.ts` — soft-delete guard (`SA-0MUJBLZC60085DI9`), `deleted-item` error.
- `src/commands/worklist.ts` — consolidated read path consumed by selection lists.
- `src/commands/next.ts` — dispatch selection path.
- `src/commands/delete.ts` — sets `deletedBy` / `status=deleted`.
- `src/commands/doctor/validate.ts` — status/stage validation.

## Related work

- **WL-0MLB703EH1FNOQR1** — "Exlude deleted from list" (completed). Covers only `status === 'deleted'`; this item covers the `deletedBy` dimension it left out. Its fix commit added no tests.
- **WL-0MV2E2ZS5001RGLO** — `wl delete` lost-update / soft-delete convergence.
- **WL-0MTFNIRXU007X7U4** — delete-side protection: unattributed deletes never override live items.
- **MS-0MW22TQS8008021W** (separate project) — residual `wl doctor` findings; the ship-comment symptom that exposed this mismatch.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** `deletedBy` is intended as the authoritative soft-delete marker (per `SA-0MUJBLZC60085DI9`), so Option A is the safer reconciliation for read paths.
- **Risk — data semantics:** changing read-path visibility affects Herdr/TUI selection lists; the change must be rolled out with the shared predicate and its tests.
- **Risk — scope:** do not alter deletion attribution or merge/sync protection logic; only reconcile the predicate.


## Impact

A user can now trust that any work item surfaced as a release candidate by `wl list --stage in_review`, `wl next`, or `wl worklist` is genuinely actionable — soft-deleted rows are never both visible and immutable, so the `dev → main` release gate no longer stalls on rows the CLI refuses to update.
data.title: Inconsistent soft-delete predicate: wl list excludes only status=deleted while wl update rejects any non-empty deletedBy (visible-but-immutable rows block the release gate)
