# Audit admission still fails closed against the shipped proxy: wrong path and wrong `available` type

## Problem statement

The proxy team shipped LP-0MW95FYMH006XYNK. Validated on 13 Nov 2026 against the live proxy at `http://192.168.0.199:8000`:

```
GET /llama/local/audit/availability  -> 200
{"cap":1,"live":0,"available":1,"leases":[],"max_audits":1}

GET /llama/local/audit/status        -> 404 {"detail":"Not Found"}
```

Two independent mismatches keep `decideAuditAvailability()` returning the fail-closed refusal for every audit offer, machine-wide:

1. **Path.** `AUDIT_AVAILABILITY_PATH` is `/llama/local/audit/status`. The proxy's shipped path is `/llama/local/audit/availability`. Its `/openapi.json` lists exactly: `/llama/local/audit/availability`, `/llama/local/audit/lease`, `/llama/local/audit/lease/renew`, `/llama/local/audit/lease/{session_id}` — no `/audit/status`.
2. **Verdict type.** The proxy sends `available` as the number `1`. `firstBoolean()` in `downtime-worker.audit-availability.contract.ts` only accepts a real `boolean`, so `parseAuditAvailabilityResponse` returns `null` for the shipped payload — fail-closed even after the path is corrected. Verified against the built parser (`packages/herdr/dist`):

```
proxy payload as shipped            -> null
same payload with available: true   -> { cap: 1, live: 0, available: true, leases: [] }
```

Effect: every root whose sprint-view head is a `completed`/`in_review` item nominates only an `audit` offer, that offer is refused with `audit-budget-unknown`, and the dispatcher has nothing to dispatch for that root. Combined with the sweep being unregistered and one-dispatch-per-tick, this is why non-AI_Hell roots have had no dispatch since mid-afternoon on 13 Nov 2026.

## Users

- **As the producer**, I want audit work to start flowing the moment the proxy advertises capacity, so finished work drains the `in_review` queues instead of sitting there indefinitely.
- **As an agent debugging a starved root**, I do not want a constant mismatch (path, value type) masquerading as a capacity refusal in the decision log.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `AUDIT_AVAILABILITY_PATH` points at the proxy's shipped endpoint (`/llama/local/audit/availability`), with a documented override (env or setting) so a future path change is a one-line change plus config, not a code edit.
- `parseAuditAvailabilityResponse` accepts the proxy's shipped verdict shape: a numeric `0`/`1` `available` (and `can_admit`) is coerced to a boolean; a real boolean is still accepted; any other value (string, null, object, 2, -1) still fails closed to `null`.
- A regression test parses the exact captured payload `{"cap":1,"live":0,"available":1,"leases":[],"max_audits":1}` at HTTP 200 and asserts `{ cap: 1, live: 0, available: true, leases: [] }`, plus a table of malformed verdicts that still resolve `null`.
- An end-to-end check against the live proxy (skipped when unreachable) asserts that `createAuditAvailabilityClient` returns `status: 'ok'` and that `decideAuditAvailability` then resolves `{ active: false, budget: { live: 0, max: 1 } }` for the current machine.
- The decision log no longer records `audit-budget-unknown` with `detail: 'http-404'` on this machine while the proxy is up, and an audit dispatch is observed (or the residual blocker is documented on the item) within one idle window.
- **Scope decision recorded:** availability-only admission is NOT race-safe across hosts, and the lease is out of scope here — lease acquisition is deferred to **WL-0MWFJH3NW006F5GN** (blocked by this item) while this item stays a bounded path and parser fix.
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` records the shipped wire contract (path, fields, verdict type), the fail-closed rules that remain, and the recorded fact that availability-only admission is a pre-check rather than a reservation (pointer to WL-0MWFJH3NW006F5GN).
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

Audits of completed work start being dispatched again instead of being refused forever, so the `in_review` queues on every project drain and their roots stop looking permanently starved.

## Constraints

- Do **not** widen this item into the lease protocol — that is WL-0MWFJH3NW006F5GN.
- The verdict coercion must stay fail-closed: only `0`/`1` numbers join the accepted set; `2`, `-1`, `"true"`, `null` and objects still resolve `null`.
- The two refusal tokens (`audit-budget-saturated`, `audit-budget-unknown`) are shared with the proxy — never rename locally.
- The contract test's reader allowlist must be updated deliberately, not widened silently.
- **Race-safety scope decision (recorded 2026-11-13, moved here from the former AC text so the
  AC stays pass/fail-able).** `GET /llama/local/audit/availability` is a point-in-time
  observation `{cap, live, available, leases}` whose own description calls it "the dispatcher's
  lease-derived availability signal" — it observes leases, it does not create one, so two hosts
  reading `live:0, available:1` in one window both dispatch (the 2026-11-03 two-audits-on-one-GPU
  race). The atomic arbiter is `POST /llama/local/audit/lease` (`200` acquired/renewed, `429`
  `audit-budget-saturated` with a bounded `retry_after_s` when a *different session* holds the
  budget, `503` `audit-budget-unavailable` on registry failure), plus `POST /audit/lease/renew`
  and `DELETE /audit/lease/{session_id}`. Single-machine concurrency is already serialised by the
  machine-wide downtime leader plus the host-budget ledger, but the audit budget is
  **cross-machine**, so only the proxy can arbitrate it atomically. **A lease is required** and is
  deferred to WL-0MWFJH3NW006F5GN.

## Desired change

Point the constant at the shipped path (with an override), teach the parser the numeric verdict, and re-state the contract as shipped rather than provisional — leaving the admission *decision* logic untouched.

## Evidence / key files

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.constants.ts` — `AUDIT_AVAILABILITY_PATH` (line 46) and the "PROVISIONAL" doc comment that must be rewritten now that LP-0MW95FYMH006XYNK has shipped.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.audit-availability.contract.ts` — `AVAILABLE_KEYS`, `firstBoolean`, `parseAuditAvailabilityResponse`.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.audit-availability.ts` — the bounded GET client.
- `packages/herdr/src/host-dispatch-budget.admission.ts` — `decideAuditAvailability` (non-`ok` outcome ⇒ `AUDIT_BUDGET_UNKNOWN_REASON` ⇒ refuse).
- Live probe: `curl -s http://192.168.0.199:8000/llama/local/audit/availability` and `/openapi.json`.

## Related work

- **LP-0MW95FYMH006XYNK** — proxy-side item, shipped (sibling project).
- **WL-0MW95GBEG005ERHS / WL-0MWAMS1PW000O3OS / WL-0MWAMSCOP003R837 / WL-0MWAMSDNW000SL0E** — completed herdr items that pinned the provisional contract, the wire types, the fail-closed client, and the admission read.
- **WL-0MVR8GDJ3008WY3Y** — registered-root sweep (currently unconfigured on this machine; the other half of the cross-root starvation).
- **WL-0MWFJH3NW006F5GN** — *Acquire a proxy audit lease before dispatch* (follow-up, discovered-from this item, blocked by it): the lease protocol that makes audit admission race-safe across hosts.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q: Is availability-only admission race-safe against concurrent herdr instances, or must a lease be acquired?**
  - **Answer (Map, self-resolved from repo + live proxy evidence — no operator input needed):** Not race-safe. The proxy's `GET /llama/local/audit/availability` is an observation (`{cap, live, available, leases}`, description: "the dispatcher's lease-derived availability signal"); it neither creates nor reserves a lease. Two hosts reading `live:0, available:1` concurrently both dispatch, which is the 2026-11-03 two-audits-on-one-GPU failure. The atomic arbiter is `POST /llama/local/audit/lease` (`429 audit-budget-saturated` when a *different session* holds the budget, `503 audit-budget-unavailable` on registry failure), which herdr does not call. Single-machine concurrency is covered by the machine-wide downtime leader (`WL-0MTII41WG009FHYN`) plus the host-budget ledger (`WL-0MVXWQFGV000D2AB`), but the audit budget is cross-machine, so only the proxy can arbitrate.
  - **Decision:** lease acquisition is **required** and is therefore **follow-up work, not scope creep** on this item — created as **WL-0MWFJH3NW006F5GN**, registered as depending on this item. This item stays a bounded path + parser fix so the starvation stops immediately.
  - **Evidence:** `curl -s http://192.168.0.199:8000/openapi.json` (paths `/llama/local/audit/{availability,lease,lease/renew,lease/{session_id}}` with the quoted descriptions); `curl -s http://192.168.0.199:8000/llama/local/audit/availability` → `{"cap":1,"live":0,"available":1,"leases":[],"max_audits":1}`; `grep -rn "/audit/lease" packages/herdr/src` → no matches; `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` § *Proxy audit availability*.
- **Q: Should the numeric verdict be coerced, or should the proxy be asked to send a boolean?**
  - **Answer (Map, self-resolved):** Coerce client-side. The proxy is shipped and `max_audits:1` in the same payload shows the served shape is stable; a tolerant client (accept `0`/`1` and `true`/`false`, reject everything else) costs one alias entry and keeps the fail-closed guarantee, while a proxy change would block the starvation fix on another release.
  - **Evidence:** captured payload above; `firstBoolean()` in `downtime-worker.audit-availability.contract.ts`; the existing alias set (`AVAILABLE_KEYS`) was designed for exactly this rename/shape tolerance.

## Plan

Decomposed into five children (test-first order). Parent ACs are covered as:
AC1 -> shipped path + override; AC2 -> numeric verdict coercion; AC3 -> regression tests (red first);
AC4/AC5 -> live-proxy end-to-end + dispatch evidence; AC6/AC7/AC8 -> documentation;
AC9 -> final full-suite gate inside the verification child.

| # | Child | Effort | Depends on |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Pin the shipped audit-availability wire contract in regression tests (test-first) — `WL-0MWFJTHZM008GZCH` | ~2 h | — |
| 2 | Point the audit-availability path at the shipped endpoint with a documented override — `WL-0MWFJTREM0050EPU` | ~1 h | #1 |
| 3 | Accept the proxy numeric 0/1 verdict and keep the parser fail-closed — `WL-0MWFJTWUA00784E7` | ~1 h | #1 |
| 4 | Prove audit admission against the live proxy and record dispatch evidence — `WL-0MWFJU0IU003D1J1` | ~1 h | #2, #3 |
| 5 | Document the shipped audit-availability wire contract and pre-check scope — `WL-0MWFJU8JP001FXDW` | ~0.5 h | #2, #3 |

Every phase is a vertical slice: each child lands code/tests/docs together (tests first, then the
constant + client, then the parser, then the live proof, then the docs rewrite). Between phases,
re-read the next child's description and update it if the live proxy or the split-guard baseline
disagrees with what is written there.

### Plan: changelog

- 2026-11-13T22:30Z (plan): created 5 children in test-first order and wired their dependency edges;
  trimmed the *Scope decision recorded* AC to a pass/fail-able statement and moved its lease-protocol
  rationale verbatim into `## Constraints`; recorded the override decision (env var, not a persisted
  setting) in the Appendix. Parent ACs unchanged otherwise.

### Plan session (2026-11-13) — additional entries

- **Q: How should the path override be exposed — an environment variable or a persisted setting?**
  - **Answer (Map, self-resolved from repo precedent — no operator input needed):** env var
    `HERDR_AUDIT_AVAILABILITY_PATH`, read per call beside the constant.
  - **Evidence:** the existing one-release knob is an env var, not a persisted file —
    `HERDR_AUDIT_LOCAL_BUDGET` (`packages/herdr/src/host-dispatch-budget.ts`, documented as "an
    environment variable (not a persisted setting) so it can be reverted without editing a file,
    matching the `HERDR_HOST_MAX_*` precedent"); the only persisted config in the machine
    coordination dir is the caps file `budget.json`. An env var keeps the documented override a
    one-line revert and needs no schema.
  - **Preferred option (advisory, for record):** env var — matches the established herdr knob
    pattern and needs no `budget.json` schema change.
- **Q: Does the fix need new barrel exports (and therefore a split-guard re-baseline)?**
  - **Answer (Map, self-resolved):** No. The resolver belongs in `downtime-worker.constants.ts`,
    which the contract test's reader allowlist already permits; the barrel export surface (frozen in
    `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.split-baseline.json`) stays untouched. Any future consumer
    that needs the resolver through the barrel must re-baseline deliberately
    (`npx tsx packages/herdr/test/split-guard/scan.ts --write-baseline`), never to make a red gate
    green.
  - **Evidence:** `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.audit-availability.contract.test.ts` (the
    `ALLOWED` reader set) and `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.split-guard.test.ts` (frozen
    baseline + documented re-baseline command).

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items

# Downtime offers: fill empty buckets from the rest of the project backlog, not just the visible list

## Problem statement

The dispatcher can only dispatch what an instance *offers*, but each herdr instance computes its offers in `computeMostImportantItem` (`packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.coordination.ts`) by partitioning its **sprint-view window only** — the live `browseItemCount`, currently 20 items — into the `implement` / `audit` / `prep` buckets. A bucket that yields no nominee inside that window nominates nothing, and the window is deliberately never widened to fill it (WL-0MWDDHQON0015T3P AC3). The existing whole-backlog extension (`fetchExtendedHerdrItems` / `fetchWholeBacklogTail`, WL-0MW9XS0XR007K1TH) feeds only the *single* legacy offer, never the nominee buckets.

Live evidence from 13 Nov 2026 (`~/.herdr/downtime/downtime-coordination.json`):

```
AI_Hell              offers=[implement, audit, prep]   ← 3 buckets
ContextHub           offers=[implement, audit, prep]   ← 3 buckets
tce-the-rising       offers=[audit]                    ← 1 bucket
SorraAgents          offers=[audit]                    ← 1 bucket
tce-main-street      offers=[audit]                    ← 1 bucket
Tableau-Card-Engine  offers=[audit]                    ← 1 bucket
```

`tce-the-rising`'s ranked head is three `plan_complete` items followed by 16 `in_review` audits; the first two plan items are filtered out (a 24 h dispatched marker and a live pane). The window's audit bucket therefore fills, the other buckets nominate nothing, and the leader has no prep or implement offer to fall through to when the audit is refused. Its backlog beyond item 20 — and every other ready item in the project — is invisible to the dispatcher.

## Users

- **As the producer**, I want each project's ready work to be reachable by the dispatcher even when it sits below the visible worklist, so projects with large backlogs stop appearing idle.
- **As an agent debugging a root that offers only audits**, I want the offer computation to explain that it widened, or that every candidate was gated.

### User stories

1. When `tce-the-rising`'s visible top 20 items contain only audits, its check-in advertises an `implement` and a `prep` nominee drawn from items 21+, so the leader has a fall-through when the audit is refused.
2. When the leader refuses an audit for the entered entry, the same entry's `prep` nominee is dispatched in the same tick (no re-offer round trip).
3. When a deeper candidate is gated (producer-review flag, dispatched marker, in-flight pane, review-queue hold), it never becomes a nominee merely because the scan went deeper.
4. When a root genuinely has nothing dispatchable in its whole backlog, the outcome is the same `noCandidate` result with the same attribution as before.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The nominee scan is no longer window-only: for each `implement` / `audit` / `prep` bucket without a nominee after the visible window is scanned, the scan continues through the geometric whole-backlog extension (reuse the existing loop over `fetchExtendedHerdrItems`, `DOWNTIME_DISPATCH_EXTEND_MAX` growth and `DOWNTIME_DISPATCH_EXTEND_MAX_ROUNDS` cap; `fetchWholeBacklogTail` is the same primitive wrapped to exhaustion and is used by the batch path, not by this function) until that bucket has a nominee or the tail is exhausted.
- The extension is a WINDOW WIDENING of the same canonical ranking (`getHerdrListHead`), never a second ranking and never a second `wl` spawn per bucket: one read path, buckets partitioned from the same ordered stream.
- Every sequential filter is applied unchanged to extended candidates: classification (producer-review gate, freshness/recency, risk/effort caps), dispatched-marker exclusion (24 h TTL), attempt budget, non-terminal cooldown, code-freeze split-by-skill, in-flight guard, and the review-queue depth hold. No filter is relaxed or reordered, and a gate-held candidate never becomes a nominee just because it is deeper.
- Cost is bounded and observable: the extension only runs when a bucket is unfilled, growth is geometric, rounds are capped, and the existing fail-open behaviour holds (an absent/`{ok:false}`/throwing extension leaves the pre-change result byte-identical and never blocks dispatch).
- A `nomineesFilledBeyondWindow` (or equivalent) signal is recorded on the check-in / decision-log entry naming which buckets needed the extension and how many extra items were read, so an operator can see a root being reached past its visible list.
- Tests (added to `packages/herdr/src/coordination-dispatch.test.ts` and any new sibling): (a) a 20-item window whose buckets are fully gated but whose tail holds one eligible `plan` and one eligible `implement` yields both nominees, in canonical order; (b) after a refused audit the same entry still dispatches its prep nominee — the fall-through the leader's phase-2 ladder already supports; (c) a tail with nothing eligible still resolves `noCandidate` with unchanged attribution; (d) the extension is not entered when the window already fills every bucket (no extra reads); (e) a `wl` failure in the extension leaves the window result unchanged.
- Docs: `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` states that the visible window bounds rendering only, and that buckets are filled from the whole ranked backlog — the "Nothing is widened to fill a bucket" paragraph is rewritten accordingly, and the "window is never widened to fill a bucket" statements in `downtime-worker.coordination.ts` (and the AC3 note in `coordination-dispatch.test.ts`) are updated.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.
- **Explicitly out of scope, recorded rather than silently absorbed:** (i) candidates held by the 24 h dispatched-marker or by a still-open in-flight pane stay invisible regardless of widening — separate items own those (they are why `RISE-0MWC9J1OD001CT26` and `RISE-0MW6M69LE004Z0QG` are not offered today); (ii) the leader's registered-root sweep (`downtimeWorklogRoots`) stays a separate, independent mechanism; (iii) the audit-admission budget fix and the round-robin charge are separate items — this change must not touch either.

## Impact

Every project can offer its dispatcher a full set of buckets drawn from its whole backlog, so a root whose visible top 20 items are all audits no longer hands the leader an empty menu while its ready work waits below the fold.

## Constraints

- One read path: bucket partitioning and the single offer must come from the same ordered stream produced by `getHerdrListHead`; no per-bucket `wl` spawn and no second ranking implementation.
- Filter order is load-bearing (it decides attribution and side effects such as `flagBudgetExhausted`); the extension must run the same `scanOfferable` chain unchanged, only over more items.
- Extra reads are paid only when needed: no widening when the window already fills every bucket, and the walk stops as soon as all buckets are filled.
- Fail-open is non-negotiable: an extension that fails or adds nothing must leave the pre-change result byte-identical (same `noCandidate` / hold tokens and attribution).
- Backwards compatibility: entries whose nominees are all window-sourced stay byte-identical; v1-era leaders keep reading `workItemId` as the first offer.
- Run-time budget: the leader tick cost must stay within the existing benchmark ceiling (`npm run benchmark:leader-tick-cost`), since the entry may now carry nominees sourced from more reads on the owner side.

## Existing state

- `computeMostImportantItem` (`downtime-worker.coordination.ts`) reads the sprint-view window once via `deps.getHerdrListHead(cwd, sprintWindow)`, then calls `scanOfferable(head.items, true, offerState)` to accumulate the single offer **and** the per-bucket nominees.
- The whole-backlog loop below it calls `scanOfferable(extendedItems, false, offerState)` — extension candidates feed only the single offer; the `withNominees:false` flag is the coded form of "the window is never widened to fill a bucket" (AC3 of WL-0MWDDHQON0015T3P, documented at `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`, "Nothing is widened to fill a bucket").
- `scanOfferable` already implements the full sequential filter chain (classification → bucket skip → dispatched marker → attempt budget → non-terminal cooldown → code-freeze → in-flight guard → review-queue hold), with first-gate-wins rejection attribution.
- `fetchExtendedHerdrItems` (gates) grows geometrically (`max(current + DOWNTIME_DISPATCH_EXTEND_MAX, current * 2)`), returns only items beyond `current`, and is fail-open; `fetchWholeBacklogTail` loops it to exhaustion under the same round cap and is used by `downtime-worker.coordination-batch.ts` — `computeMostImportantItem` runs its own equivalent loop (`DOWNTIME_DISPATCH_EXTEND_MAX_ROUNDS`) and stops at the first single offer.
- `downtime-worker.coordination-checkin.ts` writes the v2 `offers` payload from `result.nominees`, falling back to a single-offer payload when `nominees` is empty; it logs `emptyOfferLogFields(result.attribution)` on the empty path.
- `downtime-worker.coordination-leader.ts` iterates an entry's offers via `orderAdmissibleOffers` and already `continue`s to the next nominee when the audit budget refuses one.

## Desired change

When the visible list yields no nominee for a bucket, keep walking the SAME canonical ranking deeper into the project's backlog until each bucket has a nominee (or the backlog is exhausted). The visible window is a rendering bound, not a dispatch bound — the same principle already applied to the single-offer path. Concretely: run the extension whenever at least one bucket is unfilled (not only when the single offer is missing), pass the nominees flag through to the extended scan, stop as soon as all buckets are filled, and record which buckets were filled beyond the window plus how many extra items were read.

## Plan (plan skill, 13 Nov 2026)

**Decomposition decision: single leaf — no child items.** This is a Small/Medium `feature` whose ACs already enumerate the exact test cases (a)-(e), the docs edits and every touched file, and whose siblings of comparable size (`WL-0MWDDHQON0015T3P`, `WL-0MWDVMZNV0011FDT`) shipped as single items. Splitting it would duplicate the AC list across children without isolating any independently deliverable slice, so planning stops at `plan_complete` and implementation continues on this item.

### Vertical slice, test-first

One vertical slice (code + tests + docs + observability), delivered in this order:

1. **Red tests first** — extend `packages/herdr/src/coordination-dispatch.test.ts` with cases (a) and (b): a 20-item window whose buckets are all gated but whose tail holds an eligible `plan` and an eligible `implement` yields both nominees in canonical `COORDINATION_OFFER_BUCKETS` order; and a refused audit still leaves the entry's `prep` nominee dispatchable in the same tick. Cases (c), (d) and (e) are written in the same batch as regression guards (they must stay green before and after). Verify: changed-scope run via `/skill:test` fails on (a)/(b) and passes (c)/(d)/(e) pre-change.
2. **Signal plumbing (types)** — add an optional, additive field to the success variant of `MostImportantItemResult` (e.g. `filledBeyondWindow?: { buckets: CoordinationOfferKind[]; itemsRead: number }`), leaving every legacy union member untouched. Verify: build (typecheck) plus a check-in snapshot showing a window-sourced entry rendered byte-identically (field absent).
3. **Widening in `computeMostImportantItem`** — the whole-backlog loop runs while `offerState.singleOffer === null || nomineesByBucket.size < COORDINATION_OFFER_BUCKETS.length`, scans extended batches with `withNominees: true`, accumulates `itemsRead` per round **before** the early `break`, records the buckets first filled beyond the window, and stops as soon as every bucket is filled. `scanOfferable`'s own early stop stays the term-limit (single offer found AND all buckets filled). Verify: tests (a)-(e) green, plus the existing nominee/window and single-offer extension suites unchanged.
4. **Observability write** — `downtime-worker.coordination-checkin.ts` records the signal on the check-in entry and/or coordination decision-log entry (field or log fields naming buckets + items read); the `noCandidate` attribution path keeps reporting `windowSize = head.items.length + extendedTotal` exactly as today. Verify: a check-in test asserting the signal appears for a widened entry and is absent for a window-only entry.
5. **Docs and comment rewrite** — `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` "Per-bucket nominees from one head read" / "Nothing is widened to fill a bucket" (line ~170) and the window statement at ~297 become "the visible window bounds rendering only; buckets are filled from the whole ranked backlog"; the AC3 commentary in `downtime-worker.coordination.ts` (`withNominees:false` doc) and `coordination-dispatch.test.ts` (~line 1134) is rewritten to match. Verify: grep for "never widened"/"Nothing is widened" returns only the new wording.
6. **Benchmark** — re-run `npm run benchmark:leader-tick-cost` on the owner side to confirm the tick stays within the existing ceiling with more reads per entry.

Between steps 3 and 4, re-read this description and the leader-side fall-through tests: any AC now covered differently is updated before the next step starts.

### Filters, cost, and fail-open (implementation invariants)

- **One read path:** bucket partitioning and the single offer both come from `getHerdrListHead`; the extension is a window widening of the same ordered stream, one `wl` spawn per round (never per bucket).
- **Filter chain unchanged:** the extended batches go through the identical `scanOfferable` sequence (classification → bucket skip → dispatched marker → attempt budget → non-terminal cooldown → code-freeze → in-flight guard → review-queue hold), first-gate-wins attribution included.
- **Bounded:** extension entered only when at least one bucket is unfilled; geometric growth; `DOWNTIME_DISPATCH_EXTEND_MAX_ROUNDS` cap; walk stops when all buckets are filled.
- **Fail-open:** an absent/`{ok:false}`/throwing extension leaves the pre-change result (same tokens, same attribution, `nominees` unchanged) and never blocks dispatch.

### Decisions taken at plan time

- **`flagBudgetExhausted` side-effect amplification — accepted, documented in code.** Widening may now flag deeper attempt-exhausted items that were previously never visited. Gating the flag for extended candidates would make the filter chain conditional on scan depth, contradicting the "same filters, unchanged order" constraint; the flag is a producer-review marker, and the existing single-offer extension already exhibits exactly this behaviour. The implementation records this decision in a comment beside the flag call and in the docs paragraph.
- **Signal shape — union-additive.** An optional field rather than a new discriminant, so v1/v2 leaders and the check-in fallback keep byte-identical behaviour for window-only entries (see AC "Backwards compatibility").
- **`extendedTotal` accounting — unchanged on the empty path, corrected for the new signal.** `extendedTotal` is still only incremented for rounds that yield no offer, so `summariseEmptyOffer` window sizes do not shift; the new `itemsRead` counts every extended item read, including the round that filled the last bucket.

**Key Files:**

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.coordination.ts` — `computeMostImportantItem`: the whole-backlog loop currently passes `withNominees:false` and only runs when the single offer is missing; the `scanOfferable` early-stop condition and the AC3 commentary need updating. `scanOfferable`, `emitNominees`.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.types.ts` — `MostImportantItemResult` / `CoordinationNominee`: carry the "filled beyond window" signal (bucket names + items read) without changing the legacy union members.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.coordination-checkin.ts` — write the signal onto the check-in entry and/or the coordination log entry.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.gates.ts` — `fetchExtendedHerdrItems` (`fetchWholeBacklogTail` is its exhaustion wrapper for the batch path; this change reuses `fetchExtendedHerdrItems` only — likely no change beyond doc comments).
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.coordination-leader.ts` — `orderAdmissibleOffers` fall-through after a refused audit (regression coverage only).
- `packages/herdr/src/coordination-dispatch.test.ts` — nominee/window tests, including the existing "never widened" assertion near AC3 (must be rewritten).
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — "Per-bucket nominees from one head read" and "Nothing is widened to fill a bucket" paragraphs; window-bounds-rendering statement.
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher-post-fix-verification.md` — verification steps for a widened offer (if it enumerates offer evidence).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** the ranked head beyond the window is stable between reads (same ranking function, same `wl` store); a concurrently changing backlog can yield a slightly different tail — acceptable, as it already is for the single-offer extension.
- **Risk — attribution drift:** deeper candidates now produce rejection entries; `summariseEmptyOffer` window sizes must keep reporting the window that was actually scanned (the existing `extendedTotal` already accumulates this) so operator diagnostics do not shift.
- **Risk — side-effect amplification:** `scanOfferable` flags attempt-budget-exhausted items (`flagBudgetExhausted`). Widening the scan can flag items that were previously never visited; this is the same side effect the existing extension already exhibits, but it becomes more likely — review that this is acceptable or gate it (document the decision in the implementation).
- **Risk — load:** each widened round is a `wl` list spawn on the owner instance's check-in path; bounded by geometric growth and the round cap, but visible on roots with thousands of items. The leader-tick benchmark should be re-run.
- **Risk — scope creep:** related opportunities (dispatched-marker TTL, in-flight invisibility, registered-root sweep) are recorded as separate items — do not absorb them here.
- **Assumption:** `prep` buckets (`plan`/`intake`/`risk-effort`) are as eligible for widening as `implement`/`audit`; the classifier order is unchanged.

## Related work

- **WL-0MWDDHQON0015T3P** (completed) — tier-aware offers. Its AC3 ("the window is never widened to fill a bucket") is **superseded** by this item; a comment has been recorded on that item.
- **WL-0MWDVMZNV0011FDT** (completed) — per-bucket nominees from one shared head read: the structure this item extends.
- **WL-0MW9XS0XR007K1TH** (completed) — made every work item a dispatch candidate; this item extends the same principle to the nominee buckets.
- **WL-0MVR8GDJ3008WY3Y / WL-0MW4ZOSD6004SAVD** — registered-root sweep (a *cross-root* mechanism, currently unconfigured on this machine); independent of this change.
- **WL-0MWFIZ8H5005FVNN** (round-robin charge) and the audit-admission fix — the other two blockers in the 13 Nov dispatch starvation, on separate items.
- **WL-0MWC9J1OD001CT26 / WL-0MW6M69LE004Z0QG** — the two gated `tce-the-rising` plan items that motivated the evidence; out of scope here.

### Related work items (automated find-related report)

- **WL-0MWDVN2HN004CQ1O** — Leader iterates offers through unchanged filter chain with drain-aware tie-break (completed): the leader-side half this item relies on for fall-through.
- **WL-0MWDVMZNV0011FDT** — Per-bucket nominees computed from one shared head read (completed): the owner-side half being widened.
- **WL-0MWDVMVX50012RSU** — Coordination schema v2: bounded offers array with v1 migration-read (completed): the `offers` payload that will carry widened nominees unchanged.

### Related files (automated report)

- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — the offers/window documentation to update (references WL-0MWDDHQON0015T3P, WL-0MW9XS0XR007K1TH, WL-0MVR8GDJ3008WY3Y).
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — dispatcher feature notes referencing the same offer/bucket work.
- `CLI.md` — herdr CLI surface; only relevant if a diagnostic token is documented there.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q:** Does intake need a producer interview for this item? — **Answer (agent, autonomy):** No. The item was created from a completed investigation with live evidence, a desired change, explicit ACs and a documented out-of-scope list; the remaining uncertainties are implementation-level and recorded as risks. Source: item description at intake time; repo inspection of `downtime-worker.coordination.ts`, `downtime-worker.gates.ts`, `downtime-worker.coordination-checkin.ts`, `downtime-worker.coordination-leader.ts` and `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`.
- **Q:** Is `WL-0MWDDHQON0015T3P` (tier-aware offers) a duplicate of this item? — **Answer (agent):** No, partial overlap only. That item deliberately excluded per-bucket widening (its AC3); this item supersedes exactly that constraint while keeping its one-read-per-bucket partitioning. Source: `wl show WL-0MWDDHQON0015T3P`, `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` §"Per-bucket nominees from one head read".
- **Q:** Should the dispatched-marker TTL and in-flight invisibility be fixed here? — **Answer (agent):** No — explicitly out of scope, already tracked elsewhere (`RISE-0MWC9J1OD001CT26`, `RISE-0MW6M69LE004Z0QG`). Source: item description, "Explicitly out of scope".
- **Q:** Does the review-queue depth hold need to change so a deep implement can be offered? — **Answer (agent):** No. The hold stays an unchanged sequential filter; a deep implement nominee that the hold refuses must not become a nominee. Source: `scanOfferable` filter chain; `isImplementHeldByReviewGate`.

### Plan session (13 Nov 2026, agent-routed, autonomy)

- **Q:** Does this Small/Medium item need child work items, or is it small enough to implement as a single leaf? — **Answer (agent, autonomy):** Single leaf, no children. The ACs already enumerate the exact tests (a)-(e), the docs edits and every touched file, and comparably sized siblings (`WL-0MWDDHQON0015T3P`, `WL-0MWDVMZNV0011FDT`) shipped as single items; decomposition would only duplicate the AC list. Source: `wl show --children` (no children at plan time), `docs/dev/plan-skill-reference.md`, sibling item histories.
- **Q:** Should the widened scan gate `flagBudgetExhausted` so deeper attempt-exhausted items are not flagged for producer review? — **Answer (agent, autonomy):** No — accept and document. Making the flag conditional on scan depth would make the filter chain depth-dependent, contradicting the "filters applied unchanged, order load-bearing" constraint, and the existing single-offer extension already exhibits the same side effect. Recorded in the decisions block and to be noted in a code comment beside the flag call. Source: `scanOfferable` (`downtime-worker.coordination.ts` ~line 455), item "Risks & assumptions".
- **Q:** Does the "filled beyond the window" signal need a new `MostImportantItemResult` discriminant? — **Answer (agent, autonomy):** No — an optional additive field on the existing success variant, so window-only entries (and v1-era leaders reading `workItemId`) stay byte-identical. Source: `MostImportantItemResult` union in `downtime-worker.types.ts`; check-in `offers` fallback in `downtime-worker.coordination-checkin.ts`.
- **Q:** Should the widening call `fetchWholeBacklogTail` directly instead of the per-round `fetchExtendedHerdrItems` loop? — **Answer (agent, autonomy):** No — reuse the loop already in `computeMostImportantItem` so each round's newly visible items are scanned incrementally and the walk can stop mid-tail as soon as all buckets are filled; `fetchWholeBacklogTail` exhausts the tail and is used by the batch path. Source: `downtime-worker.gates.ts` (`fetchExtendedHerdrItems`, `fetchWholeBacklogTail`), `downtime-worker.coordination-batch.ts` line ~96.

# RCA: the worklist header reported `implement 3/6` while 10 implement dispatches were running

## Symptom

The worklist header segment `[budget: implement n/max · audit n/max]`
(`packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`, fed by `host-budget-status.ts`) reported
`implement 3/6` on 2026-11-13 ~21:55 while `herdr pane list` showed **10**
running implement dispatches across four projects.

## Measurement (reproduced from the live host)

```
ledger ~/.herdr/downtime/dispatch-budget.json: 4 implement entries
  AH-0MW0KSCU20096B02  w50:p64  pane DEAD   started 19:27:53
  AH-0MW25VH540078FDK  w50:p65  pane live   started 20:07:33
  SA-0MWE4BT63005N8OE  w57:pMC  pane live   started 21:38:36
  WL-0MWDD2JE6006CL7I  w5M:p72  pane live   started 21:40:54
live implement-labelled panes: 10   (w50:p65, w50:p5B, w50:p5N, w50:p5Q,
  w50:p5Y, w50:p50, w50:p62, w5M:p72, w57:pMC, w5S:p4J)
budget.json: maxImplement 6
```

The number is not a count of running work: it is the count of machine-ledger
entries that (a) exist, (b) are confirmed (carry a `paneId`), (c) whose pane is
in the live pane list, and (d) are not stale-and-dead. Six running dispatches
had been confirmed (each has a dispatch-log enrichment row carrying its pane
id), yet had no ledger entry, so the ledger had silently lost them.

## Root causes (see the child items)

1. `release(itemId)` is the only release primitive and is keyed on the item id
   alone, so any aborted dispatch attempt or any pane close for an item deletes
   *any* entry for that item, including one belonging to a still-running
   dispatch (`anchor-unavailable` alone fired 211 times that day).
2. `repairLedgerFromLivePanes` is triggered *automatically* by any
   not-fully-valid ledger read and rewrites the whole document from live panes,
   but only reconstructs panes whose title starts with `Downtime` — which
   excludes `⚠️`/`🚫`-decorated and `Manually triggered` panes (6 of the 10
   live implement panes that day).
3. Nothing reconciles the ledger against live panes: the display is read-only by
   design, and the dead-pane sweep runs only from the pane-close reaper (which
   had not run since 12 Nov), so a dead entry (`w50:p64`) lingers while a live
   pane's entry is missing.
4. Ledger mutations are unaudited, so individual deletions cannot be attributed
   (this is why the RCA could not be closed conclusively).

## Impact (why this is not cosmetic)

The same under-counted `live` figure is what admission compares with
`maxImplement` (`host-dispatch-budget.admission.ts`), so the cap is effectively
unenforced — 10 implement panes against a cap of 6, with no
`host-budget-implement` refusal logged all day. The header is faithfully
reporting a ledger that has drifted.

## Scope

Ledger identity/retention, counting truthfulness, reconciliation cadence and
observability. **Out of scope:** generalising the budget to all
`DowntimeSkillKind` members (WL-0MW50EHZ6007QBPB) and the proxy-owned audit
budget contract.

## Acceptance Criteria

- No dispatch's confirmed entry can be deleted by another dispatch attempt, by
  another kind, or by another pane for the same work item.
- No confirmed entry is ever dropped without a durable, queryable record of the
  deletion (operation, reason, actor, item, pane).
- The worklist counter and admission both agree with the observed set of live
  implement panes within one reconciliation cadence, demonstrated against the
  2026-11-13 state (10 live panes must read 10, not 3).
- Repair from live panes is never triggered automatically by an admission read,
  and an operator-initiated repair reconstructs every live downtime pane
  regardless of label decoration.
- Reconciliation runs on the worker tick with a bounded cadence and surfaces its
  failures instead of swallowing them.

## Impact

Operators can trust the worklist's in-flight count and the host dispatch cap
again: the number shown matches the dispatches actually running, and the cap
actually stops new work at `maxImplement` instead of letting the host run
double the configured limit.

## Headline

A driven child's pre-push full-suite gate must judge only the mutation its own
run could have caused — currently a concurrent session's mid-run writes to the
shared main checkout are misattributed to the suite and block the push.

## Summary

A driven child's `implement.py finish` is refused when the pre-push full-suite
gate observes another live session's uncommitted edits in the **main checkout**.
The gate reports `live_repo_mutation` ("the test suite changed a guarded
checkout") and fails the run, so the push is refused — even though the child's
own worktree is clean and its commit is composed only of its own files.

Observed while finishing WL-0MWETWFSH007GRTR (tests-only, worktree clean,
changed-scope green): the full-suite gate failed with

```text
live-repo mutation detected: the test suite changed a guarded checkout for .../worktrees/wl-WL-0MWETWFSH...
  in main checkout /home/rgardler/projects/ContextHub:
  added path [ M] docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md
  added path [ M] packages/herdr/src/downtime-log-storage.ts
  added path [??] packages/herdr/src/host-dispatch-budget.audit.test.ts
  added path [??] packages/herdr/src/host-dispatch-budget.audit.ts
  added path [ M] packages/herdr/src/host-dispatch-budget.ts
```

Evidence that the mutation is concurrent agent activity, not the suite:
`packages/herdr/src/host-dispatch-budget.audit.test.ts` has mtime 22:42:45,
four seconds *after* the suite started at 22:42:41, and the paths belong to the
host-dispatch-budget workstream (WL-0MWFJD1RV008FCCR, held by
`herdr-1794608223-1882173-11244`, driving children from ~22:17). No test in this
repo writes `.ts` sources.

## Users

- **Driven implementer agent (finishing a child in its worktree).** As an
  implementing agent I want my finish gate to judge only the mutation my own run
  could have caused, so I am not blocked by another session's unrelated work in
  the shared main checkout.
- **Operator / maintainer.** As an operator I want a gate failure to name the
  owning session or work item, so I know who is writing the checkout and do not
  hunt a phantom bug in a clean tree.
- **Downtime dispatcher.** As the dispatcher I do not want a false gate failure
  to burn a retry slot or re-dispatch work that is already correct.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The gate distinguishes changes that were pre-existing before the run, or made
  by another live session, from changes the suite made during this run, and
  fails the run only on the latter (the verdict is derived from a start-of-run
  snapshot of the guarded checkout, never from an unqualified `HEAD`/`git
  status` comparison).
- A driven child whose own worktree is clean and whose changed-scope gate
  passed is not blocked by unrelated dirty paths in the main checkout.
- When the gate does fail, the report names the owning session/work item where
  one is discoverable (e.g. via `.implement_state.json`, claimed items, or the
  main-checkout lock holder), instead of implying the running item corrupted the
  tree.
- A genuine suite-caused mutation of a guarded checkout — above all a
  tracked-file deletion/wipe in the main checkout (the 2026-10-26
  `packages/shared` incident class) — still fails the run: the fix narrows the
  false positive without weakening that protection.
- Regression tests cover both directions: (a) a dirty main checkout with a clean
  child worktree ⇒ the gate passes and reports the foreign paths as
  informational; (b) the suite mutating the guarded checkout during the run ⇒
  the gate fails and names the paths.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
  comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

Agents stop chasing a phantom corruption bug when a concurrent session has the
main checkout dirty, and driven children are no longer blocked by work they
never touched.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk: masking a real wipe.** Narrowing the main-checkout surface (option A)
  could let a suite-caused *addition* through. Mitigation: the deletion/wipe
  class (the actual incident) stays verdict-bearing, and the finish
  main-checkout guard (WL-0MVPE2CMY/CZ family) remains a second net.
- **Risk: actor attribution is unreliable.** Mid-run writes carry no ownership
  metadata git can read; probing `.implement_state.json`/claimed items is
  best-effort. Assumption: attribution is informational and always falls back to
  "unknown" rather than becoming a new failure mode.
- **Risk: pin/test churn.** Changing the clean→dirty direction moves a pinned
  characterisation test and a documented blind spot; the change must update
  rule, docs and pin together (see Constraints).
- **Risk: scope creep.** Options B/C expand into actor-attribution plumbing and
  isolated-worktree migration. Mitigation: keep this item to the false-positive
  verdict; record the isolated-worktree migration under WL-0MW4W15U500009D2 and
  any actor-attribution enhancement as separate linked work.
- **Assumption:** the guarded run's own worktree is the only checkout the suite
  can legitimately write; the main checkout is shared and may be written by
  other live sessions at any time.
- **Assumption:** "live session" is not directly observable; attribution uses
  whatever durable evidence exists (state files, claimed items, lock holder) and
  degrades to "unknown".

## Constraints

- **Do not weaken the wipe protection.** The main-checkout coverage exists
  because a worktree-scoped suite wiped every tracked file of `packages/shared`
  on 2026-10-26 (WL-0MVPE2BY9001CR9O, WL-0MVPADZ1Z000FOSG). Tracked-file
  deletions in the main checkout must still fail the run.
- **Conflicting documented design decision.** The working-tree attribution rule
  (SA-0MUIJAHXS003M7BG, `docs/dev/test-isolation.md` §8.5) **deliberately
  retains** the clean→dirty direction as a mutation, pinned by
  `TestWorkingTreeAttributionBoundaries::test_clean_to_dirty_is_a_retained_move_direction`
  and documented as blind spot #2. Any change to that direction must update the
  rule, the doc section and the pin together in one change.
- **Plumbing-only derivations.** The guard's derivations must stay git-plumbing
  only (status codes + the start snapshot) — never a `wl-*` or path-name
  heuristic. If actor evidence is introduced, it must be an explicit, documented
  second signal, not a substitute for the plumbing rule.
- **Exactly one guard owner.** `guarded_run_all` is the single outer guard owner;
  the inner `live_repo_guard` plugin must apply the same rule and must not fork
  it.
- **Bounded cost.** The guard stays read-only git plumbing with no per-test work
  (the per-test fingerprint remains a trigger, never a verdict).
- **Fail closed.** `implement.py finish` must never push a checkout that a
  suite-caused mutation corrupted; narrowing the false positive must not turn a
  genuine mutation green.
- **CHANGELOG.md excluded** — managed by the ship skill's release pipeline.

## Existing state

- `guarded_run_all` (`skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py`) snapshots every guarded
  root before the run (`snapshot_guarded_roots`: the worktree plus, when it is a
  linked worktree, its main checkout) and diffs afterwards
  (`diff_guarded_roots` → `diff_snapshots`). `_detect_live_repo_mutation` renders
  the verdict; `implement.py`'s finish gate delegates to `guarded_run_all` and
  classifies `live_repo_mutation` as `GATE_FAILURE_INFRASTRUCTURE`.
- Attribution is **start-of-run provenance**: a path that was dirty at start and
  clean at end is excluded and reported under `live_repo_excluded`; a path that
  was **clean at start and dirty at end** (`status.added`) or is still dirty with
  a different code (`status.changed`) fails the run.
- The observed failure is the **clean→dirty direction**: the concurrent session
  wrote `.ts` sources into the main checkout *during* the run (mtime four
  seconds after the suite started), so the start-of-run snapshot was clean and
  the end snapshot showed them as `added path`.
- A single-owner lock exists for the main checkout during **finish**
  (WL-0MVPE2DA7007WF84), but it does not stop a non-finish session (a driven
  child or the operator) writing the main checkout mid-run.
- A related alternative mitigation is already scoped: run the post-push/audit
  full suite in a pinned isolated worktree (WL-0MW4W15U500009D2, blocked; its
  tests in WL-0MW4W0WDF005Y0TQ, intake_complete).

## Desired change

**Outcome:** a driven child whose own worktree is clean is not blocked by another
live session's mid-run writes to the main checkout; a genuine suite-caused
mutation (especially a tracked-file deletion/wipe in the main checkout) still
fails the run; and a failure names the owning session/work item when
discoverable.

**Mechanism is an open design question (Appendix Q1).** Candidate approaches
(not prescriptive — the plan stage must confirm):

- **(A) Narrow the main checkout's verdict surface** to the damage class the
  suite can plausibly cause — tracked-file **deletions** and modifications of
  files that were clean at start — and report concurrent **additions/untracked
  creations** as informational, naming the owning session where discoverable.
  Keeps the wipe protection, removes the dominant false positive.
- **(B) Keep the full status surface, add actor attribution** (owning session /
  work item from `.implement_state.json`, claimed items, or the main-checkout
  lock holder) and fail only when a change cannot be attributed to a foreign
  live session.
- **(C) Run the pre-push full-suite gate in an isolated worktree** pinned to the
  would-be-commit (folds into WL-0MW4W15U500009D2), so main-checkout churn is
  out of scope entirely.
- **(D) Scope the verdict to the guarded root only** when the run started in a
  worktree, reporting main-checkout churn informationally — weakest option;
  regresses the 2026-10-26 protection, so not recommended.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — `guarded_run_all`,
  `_detect_live_repo_mutation`, verdict → `live_repo_mutation` /
  `live_repo_excluded`.
- `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py` — `snapshot_guarded_roots`,
  `diff_guarded_roots`, `diff_snapshots` attribution rule,
  `describe_guarded_diff`, `excluded_churn_notes`.
- `skill/shared/live_repo_guard.py` — inner pytest plugin; applies the same rule
  and must not fork it.
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — finish test gate,
  `_adapt_guarded_result`, `_gate_failure_reason`.
- `skill/shared/tests/test_git_sandbox.py` — `TestWorkingTreeAttribution*`
  pins; the clean→dirty pin must move with the rule.
- `skill/test/tests/test_guarded_run_all.py` — outer-guard end-to-end tests
  (add the dirty-main/clean-worktree pass and the genuine-mutation fail).
- `docs/dev/test-isolation.md` §8.5 — attribution rule and blind spots.
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — finish-gate and guard-ownership
  documentation.

## Related work

From `/skill:find-related` (automated report):

- **WL-0MVPE2BY9001CR9O** (completed) — added the main-checkout guard this
  item's false positive fires from.
- **WL-0MVPE2CMW006K25Q** (completed) — finish aborts loudly on foreign
  main-checkout deletions; already names the concurrent actor on the *finish*
  guard surface.
- **WL-0MVPE2DA7007WF84** (completed) — single-owner lock for the main checkout
  during finish; does not cover non-finish writers.
- **WL-0MW4W15U500009D2** (blocked) — redirect post-push verification full-suite
  runs to a pinned isolated worktree; the architectural alternative to (C).
- **WL-0MW4W0WDF005Y0TQ** (intake_complete) — regression tests for the
  isolated-worktree verification run.
- **SA-0MUIJAHXS003M7BG** — the working-tree attribution rule (start-of-run
  provenance); the design decision this item asks to revisit for the
  clean→dirty direction.
- **WL-0MWFJD1RV008FCCR** — the concurrent host-dispatch-budget workstream whose
  writes triggered the observed failure.
- **WL-0MWETWFSH007GRTR** (completed) — the driven child whose finish was
  blocked by the false positive.
- **WL-0MV5MYBKJ0033P8U**, **WL-0MV981ZGA007ARPG** (completed) — the concurrent
  `dev`/`origin/*` ref-exclusion regressions that must stay green.
- Docs: `docs/dev/test-isolation.md` §8.5, `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md`,
  `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md`.

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 (OPEN QUESTION) — which attribution mechanism?** AC1's suggested
  mechanism ("compare against a start-of-run snapshot of the guarded checkout, not
  against `HEAD`") is **already implemented** in `guarded_run_all` /
  `diff_snapshots`. The observed failure is the clean→dirty direction — a foreign
  session wrote files into the main checkout *during* the run — which the
  documented rule (SA-0MUIJAHXS003M7BG, `test-isolation.md` §8.5 blind spot #2)
  deliberately retains as a mutation and pins with a characterisation test. A pure
  start-of-run snapshot cannot tell a mid-run foreign write from a suite write.
  Which approach should the plan adopt?
  (A) Narrow the main checkout's verdict to tracked-file deletions/modifications
  and report concurrent additions informationally;
  (B) keep the full surface and add actor attribution;
  (C) move the gate to an isolated worktree pinned to the would-be-commit
  (folds into WL-0MW4W15U500009D2);
  (D) guard only the worktree root (not recommended).
  **Recommended: (A)** — it keeps the 2026-10-26 deletion/wipe protection while
  removing the dominant false positive (concurrent additions/untracked files) at
  low plumbing-only cost; (C) is the strongest long-term fix but is a separate,
  already-scoped item.
  Source: intake research 2026-11-15; no producer answer yet.

  **Answer (producer):** A with a filed follow up for C- **Q2 — how much actor detail is required on failure?** AC2 requires naming the
  owning session/work item "where discoverable". Which evidence sources are
  acceptable? (a) `.implement_state.json` / claimed work items only;
  (b) add the main-checkout lock holder metadata; (c) best-effort plus
  "unknown".
  **Recommended: (c)** — best-effort from (a) and (b), falling back to
  "unknown", so attribution never becomes a new failure mode.
  Source: intake research 2026-11-15; no producer answer yet.

  **Answer (producer):** C- **Q3 — should this item fold into the isolated-worktree item?** Option (C)
  largely duplicates WL-0MW4W15U500009D2, which is blocked. Should this item
  stay narrow (false-positive attribution on the live guard) and leave the
  isolated-worktree migration to that item?
  **Recommended: keep this item narrow** — it fixes the gate's verdict on
  today's live-checkout path; the isolated-worktree migration is a separate
  architectural change with its own regression tests.
  Source: intake research 2026-11-15; no producer answer yet.
  **Answer (producer):** keep narrow

## Plan (2026-11-21)

**Approved mechanism:** option **(A)** — narrow the **main checkout**'s verdict surface
(producer answer to Q1: "A with a filed follow up for C"). The isolated-worktree follow-up (C)
is already filed as **WL-0MW4W15U500009D2** (blocked), with its regression tests in
**WL-0MW4W0WDF005Y0TQ** — no duplicate is created here. Actor detail is option **(c)**
(producer answer to Q2: best-effort evidence with an explicit `unknown` fallback,
informational only). This item stays narrow (producer answer to Q3).

### Repo boundary (decides where every child is implemented)

Every file in **Key Files** lives in the **SorraAgents** skill tree, not in ContextHub:

- `~/.pi/agent/skills` → `/home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents/skill`
- `ContextHub/skill/shared` is a gitignored symlink to that tree (`.gitignore:182`), so
  `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py` and friends are **not** ContextHub source.
- `docs/dev/test-isolation.md` and `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` are SorraAgents docs.

Delivery follows the precedent set by WL-0MVPE2BY9001CR9O (same guard, implemented from a WL
item: commit `1a4ad6a87` landed on SorraAgents `dev` with the WL id in the message). Children
therefore commit and run their suites in the **SorraAgents** checkout; ContextHub source is
untouched by this item.

### Features and sequencing (test-first)

| # | Item | Type | Depends on |
|---|---|---|---|
| F1 | Test: main-checkout churn verdict pins (WL-0MWR1OUF7009FG4I) | task | — |
| F2 | Role-scope the guard's verdict surface (WL-0MWR1OXHX001KJC6) | feature | F1 |
| F3 | Name the concurrent actor on failures (WL-0MWR1OYAJ000UVJS) | feature | F1 |
| F4 | Wire narrowed verdict through both guards (WL-0MWR1P1F3008AH3V) | feature | F2, F3 |
| F5 | Document role-scoped attribution and blind spots (WL-0MWR1P26Y004CYE9) | docs | F2, F4 |
| F6 | Full-suite verification and regression triage (WL-0MWR1P2ZQ009J5OV) | task | F4, F5 |

### The rule the plan adopts (derived from answer A, see Appendix Q4)

Role-scoped in `diff_guarded_roots` — the only function that knows each root's `role`, so the
outer guard and the inner plugin inherit one rule instead of forking it:

- **Guarded root** (the run's own worktree / non-linked root): **unchanged** from
  `docs/dev/test-isolation.md` §8.5 — every clean→dirty modification, deletion or creation is
  verdict-bearing.
- **Main checkout**: a newly dirty path is verdict-bearing **only** when its end status code
  reports a tracked-file deletion (`D` in either column) — the 2026-10-26 `packages/shared`
  wipe class. Newly modified (` M`, `M `, `MM`), untracked (`??`), staged additions (`A `) and
  deletion-free code transitions move to an excluded bucket, reported informationally with the
  best-effort owner.
- **Unchanged everywhere:** pre-existing-dirty→clean resolution stays excluded; refs and config
  stay fully verdict-bearing on both roots; the per-test fingerprint stays a superset trigger.

Note that a narrowing that kept *modifications* verdict-bearing in the main checkout
(only excluding untracked additions) would **not** fix the reported incident — 3 of its 5
paths were ` M` — so this plan narrows to the deletion class and relies on the two remaining
nets (full-surface guarded root, finish main-checkout guard) for modifications.

### Vertical slices

Each implementation item carries its own regression tests **and** its own docstring rule
statement (code + test + docs in one slice): F2 the helper rule and pins, F3 the helper, its
unit tests and the docstring, F4 the wiring plus end-to-end assertions. F5 is the user-facing
reference documentation that must land in the same change set because §8.5 currently documents
the opposite rule and pins it. F6 is the suite-level proof. Between phases, review and update
the next item's description before implementing it.

### Changelog

- 2026-11-21: plan created — 6 children (F1–F6), 8 dependency edges wired, effort/risk
  pre-check returned `plan` (Medium/Medium), approval gate not required.

## Appendix addendum (plan, 2026-11-21)

- **Q4 (derived, not open) — does option A still fix the reported incident?** The prose for
  option (A) said "tracked-file deletions **and modifications of files that were clean at
  start**" stay verdict-bearing while concurrent additions are informational. But the observed
  2026-11-13 failure listed three ` M` modifications created mid-run by the sibling session
  (`docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`, `packages/herdr/src/downtime-log-storage.ts`,
  `packages/herdr/src/host-dispatch-budget.ts`) plus two `??` untracked files. Keeping
  clean→dirty *modifications* verdict-bearing in the main checkout would leave the reported
  failure unfixed, contradicting AC2 ("not blocked by unrelated dirty paths in the main
  checkout") and the item's Impact. **Resolution adopted by this plan:** in the main checkout the
  verdict-bearing class is **tracked-file deletions only** (the wipe class the protection
  exists for); modifications, untracked files and staged additions are reported informationally
  with the discovered owner. Evidence: AC1/AC2/AC4 text, the incident's `added path [ M]` lines,
  `docs/dev/test-isolation.md` §8.5 blind spot #2, and the producer's Q1 answer ("A with a filed
  follow up for C").
- **Q5 (derived, not open) — where does the follow-up for option (C) live?** Already filed as
  WL-0MW4W15U500009D2 (blocked; regression tests in WL-0MW4W0WDF005Y0TQ), so the plan links it
  rather than creating a duplicate. Source: producer answer to Q1.

## Summary

`implement.py finish` fast-forwards the local `dev` branch to the about-to-be-pushed tip **before** the push succeeds, and restores it on failure. A concurrent `implement.py start` that runs inside that window resolves `dev` to the unpushed commit and creates its worktree/branch from it — permanently grafting another item's commit onto the new branch.

Observed on 2026-11-13:

- WL-0MWETWFSH007GRTR's finish created commit `e2291be45` (tests-only) and moved local `dev` to it before its push gate failed; finish then restored `dev` to `079948694`.
- `git reflog show wl-WL-0MWFJDGXQ001OXP8-append-only-audit-trail-for-budget-ledge` shows a single entry: `e2291be45 … branch: Created from dev` — i.e. the sibling child's worktree was created from the transient, unpushed tip.
- That branch is now `[ahead 1]` of `dev` with a foreign commit as its base, so its first push to `dev` will carry WL-0MWETWFSH007GRTR's commit under the wrong item id (or dump both in one push).

## Acceptance Criteria

- `finish` never moves the local `dev` ref while a push is in flight; the post-push fast-forward happens only after `git push` reports success
- On a failed/refused push, local `dev` is provably unchanged from its pre-finish value (no write-then-restore window)
- `implement.py start` resolves its base from `origin/dev` (fetched) rather than a locally mutable `dev`, or refuses to branch from a `dev` that is not a known pushed tip
- Regression test: simulate a mid-push `start` and assert the new branch's base is the pushed tip, never an unpushed sibling commit
- Full test suite passes

## Key Files

- skill/implement/scripts/implement.py (finish push + dev sync; start base resolution)

## Impact

A new child's branch can no longer inherit another work item's unpushed commit, so each push to `dev` contains exactly the work item's own changes.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MV5FDJE30088GGY** – implement.py finish: NameError 'cwd' in non-fast-forward rebase-retry path (completed)
- **WL-0MUYTCF4L000FX3M** – implement.py finish fails non-fast-forward when dev advances during the run (completed)
- **WL-0MW2A3NAP0088IE9** – Pre-push hook template: bind the full-suite gate to the pushed commit (--gate-commit) (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — matched: 0mwfjdgxq001oxp8, acceptance, ahead, another, append (+91 more)
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — matched: acceptance, ahead, another, append, assert (+91 more)
- `CHANGELOG.md` — matched: acceptance, ahead, another, audit, base (+74 more)

# Children survive deletion of their parent work item and become unreachable orphans

> **Migrated** from the SorraAgents worklog item **SA-0MW7Z1PR20094WIS** (2026-11-13) after the producer approved migrating it here, accepting the re-scope and deleting the SorraAgents original. Provenance for the orphan census below is the SorraAgents worklog; the engineering scope is entirely in this repository.

## Summary

Deleting a parent work item does not dispose of its open children. They survive as **orphans**: their `parentId` points at an id that no longer resolves (or resolves only to a soft-deleted item), so they appear in no rollup, are never closed by the parent's closure path, and are invisible to every parent-level report.

## Evidence (2026-11-08 SorraAgents backlog review)

55 of 444 open-scope items had an unresolvable parent:

| Lost parent | Resolution | Open children |
|---|---|---|
| `SA-0MSC7QZQL006Q747` | hard-deleted (id not found at all) | 46 |
| `SA-0MLDAXNBQ17OA9PT` "Scheduler Configuration & Scoping" | soft-deleted | 5 |
| `SA-0MLPU8H3B1LWK3B3` "Add closing of work item to cleanup skill" | soft-deleted | 3 |
| `SA-0ML7NOSHP0MJC6HS` "AMPA Daemon: Discord heartbeat & notifier" | soft-deleted | 1 |

The 46 hard-deleted orphans were all refactor findings from 2026-08-02, filed under a scan-batch parent that was removed while its children stayed behind; the oldest were 258 days old. None surfaced in any progress view, and none could be closed by the normal "parent closes when all children close" path — the parent was already gone.

`wl delete` is recursive by default (documented), and `--no-recursive` is the documented "leaving children orphaned" opt-out, but a hard delete evidently bypassed the children; the exact route that produced the 46-item batch is confirmed below as `wl doctor prune` / `foreign-items --apply` (see R1).

## Re-scope (producer-approved 2026-11-13)

Investigation of this repo (main @ `77264ee6a`) shows the original acceptance criteria are **substantially shipped**, which narrows the work:

- **Recursive delete ships.** `wl delete` is recursive by default, has an explicit `--no-recursive` opt-out, records `--reason`, and reports the deleted descendants — `src/commands/delete.ts` (WL-0MQFZ81MO000QSRL).
- **Doctor already flags orphans.** Root `wl doctor` (`validate`) emits a distinct per-item finding via `validateParentReferences()`: code `parent.missing-endpoint`, type `missing-parent`, carrying the lost parent id in `context.parentId` and a safe `parentId: null` proposed fix — `src/doctor/parent-check.ts`, `src/commands/doctor/validate.ts`.
- **Promotion path exists.** `wl doctor dangling-parents [--apply]` detects dangling parents and detaches them (`parentId -> null`) — `src/commands/doctor/dangling-parents.ts` (WL-0MUJM2LV1000IHKR), and `wl update <id> --parent null` detaches instead of writing `WL-NULL`.

The remaining defects are therefore narrower than the originally filed five ACs:

- **R1 — hard-delete admin paths still orphan children silently.** `wl doctor prune` hard-deletes each candidate via `store.deleteWorkItem(id)` with no descendant handling (`src/commands/doctor/prune.ts`); `wl doctor foreign-items --apply` (`applyForeignItemCleanup`, `src/doctor/foreign-items-check.ts`) likewise deletes each id individually and, although it cascades audit results and FTS entries, it neither cascades to nor refuses when an own-prefix child points at the deleted id.
- **R2 — promotion/detach loses the history.** `wl doctor dangling-parents --apply` contains no comment/attribution call, and neither `wl doctor --fix` nor `wl update <id> --parent null` records the previous parent or the rationale.
- **R3 — orphan reporting is not grouped.** Findings are emitted per child; there is no grouped summary keyed by lost-parent id carrying the count and child ids.
- **R3b — children of a *soft-deleted* parent are not reported at all.** `validateParentReferences` resolves `parentId` against `db.getAll()`, which includes soft-deleted rows (proved by `prune` filtering `status === 'deleted'` out of the same collection), so a soft-deleted parent looks resolvable. 9 of the 55 evidence orphans fell in this class.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Every hard-delete admin path that can leave children without a resolvable parent (notably `wl doctor prune`; audit `wl doctor foreign-items --apply` and any other store-level `deleteWorkItem` caller) either cascades to descendants or refuses without an explicit opt-in, so no silent orphaning remains.
2. Any explicit orphaning opt-in (`wl delete --no-recursive`) records a comment on each orphaned child naming the previous parent and the explicit decision.
3. `wl doctor` reports orphans as a distinct finding that includes the lost-parent id and the child id — including children whose parent is soft-deleted (R3b); `wl doctor dangling-parents --dry-run` summarises the grouped count of children per lost-parent id.
4. Promotion (`parentId -> null`, via `wl doctor --fix`, `wl doctor dangling-parents --apply`, or `wl update --parent null`) records a comment naming the previous parent and the rationale (promote-because-live vs retire-because-stale), so the history is not lost.
5. The retention rule — promote when the child's subject is still live; retire when it is superseded, its target is gone, or the abandoned parent's feature was never delivered — is documented alongside the remediation path.
6. Automated tests cover: pruning a parent with children does not orphan them; explicit orphaning records the previous parent; doctor output names the lost parent and the children (including the soft-deleted-parent case); promotion clears `parentId`, keeps the children reachable, and records the comment.
7. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes (CLI/doctor docs and the remediation/retention guidance).
8. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

Work can no longer disappear from every view because its parent was removed, so nothing sits in the queue invisible and unclosable.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption (now evidenced):** the 46-item hard-deleted batch came from a single-id hard-delete admin path — `wl doctor prune` is the leading candidate; `foreign-items --apply` can produce the same shape for own-prefix children.
- **Risk:** changing prune/foreign-items cascade behaviour could delete more than intended — mitigate with a dry-run-first default and an explicit opt-in for destructive cascades.
- **Risk (scope creep):** incidental doctor/delete cleanups discovered during the fix should be filed as separate items, not folded in.
- The delete-reason attribution defect is already fixed by **WL-0MW8078CA006Q2P7** (completed) and is out of scope here; do not re-open or re-implement it.

## Constraints

- Do **not** re-implement already-shipped behaviour (recursive `wl delete`, the `parent.missing-endpoint` doctor finding, `--parent null` detach); build only the residual gaps R1–R3b.
- CHANGELOG is managed by the ship release pipeline, not this item.

## Existing state

- `wl delete` recursive-by-default with `--no-recursive` and `--reason` (`src/commands/delete.ts`; WL-0MQFZ81MO000QSRL).
- `wl doctor` root `validate` includes `validateParentReferences()` → `parent.missing-endpoint` / `missing-parent` findings with a safe `parentId: null` fix (`src/doctor/parent-check.ts`, `src/commands/doctor/validate.ts`).
- `wl doctor dangling-parents [--dry-run|--apply]` detaches dangling parents (`src/commands/doctor/dangling-parents.ts`, WL-0MUJM2LV1000IHKR).
- `wl doctor prune` hard-deletes a single id via `store.deleteWorkItem(id)` with no descendant handling (`src/commands/doctor/prune.ts`) — the residual orphaning route.
- `wl doctor foreign-items --apply` hard-deletes with a "full cascade" limited to audit results + FTS entries (`src/doctor/foreign-items-check.ts`).

## Desired change

Close the residual gaps: make hard-delete admin paths cascade-or-refuse (R1), record the previous parent + decision whenever a child is orphaned or promoted (R2), and report orphans grouped by lost-parent id — including soft-deleted parents — in `wl doctor` output (R3/R3b), with a documented retention/remediation rule and tests.

- `src/doctor/parent-check.ts` — treat soft-deleted parents as unresolvable; emit the grouped orphan finding (lost-parent id, count, child ids).
- `src/commands/doctor/validate.ts` — grouped orphan summary and comment-on-detach for `--fix`.
- `src/commands/doctor/dangling-parents.ts` — grouped count per lost parent in `--dry-run` and comment on detach in `--apply`.
- `src/commands/delete.ts` — comment on each child when `--no-recursive` orphaning is applied.
- `src/commands/update.ts` — comment on `--parent null` detach naming the previous parent.
- `CLI.md`, `DOCTOR_AND_MIGRATIONS.md` — retention rule and remediation path.

## Proposed decomposition (plan input — not yet created)

Test-first ordering; each is a vertical slice (code + tests + docs):

1. **Orphan-guard failing test fixtures** (task, test-first) — shared fixtures for a hard-deleted parent, a soft-deleted parent, a foreign-prefix parent with an own child, and a promotion; tests assert the target behaviours and fail on current main.
2. **Hard-delete paths cascade-or-refuse** (R1, AC1) — `wl doctor prune` refuses (or requires an explicit `--cascade-children` opt-in) when a candidate still has live children; same audit for `foreign-items --apply`; regression tests + `DOCTOR_AND_MIGRATIONS.md`.

4. **Attribution comments on orphan/promote** (R2, AC2/AC4) — `wl delete --no-recursive` comments each orphaned child; `wl update --parent null`, `dangling-parents --apply` and `doctor --fix` comment naming the previous parent plus the promote-vs-retire rationale; tests.
5. **Retention & remediation docs** (AC5/AC7) — document the promote-when-live / retire-when-superseded rule alongside the remediation path in `CLI.md` and `DOCTOR_AND_MIGRATIONS.md`; AC8 is verified at the dev-push gate.

Producer answers on the three intake questions: **Q1 confirmed** — the sentinel/empty push refusal is absolute (fires even if the sentinel email hypothetically equalled the configured identity or an allow-list entry; policy forbids that state, pinned by SorraAgents `tests/test_author_gate_allowlist.py`). **Q2 confirmed** — the guard covers both worklog-data push paths (`wl sync` push AND `rewriteAndForcePushDataFile`, the `wl doctor foreign-items --apply --push` force-rewrite). **Q3 resolved** — tracked here in the ContextHub worklog; plan children live under this item and implement directly in this repository.

Planning is complete (`plan_complete`): see the plan-completion comment and the children. Full original brief follows verbatim.
